definition_zh: 同意；应允；就任；加入（条约）
definition_en: to agree to a request, to take up a high office, or to become a party to a treaty
core_image: 一扇关着的门，有人在里面点头，门才打开
scene: 代表们在门外等了很久，直到里面终于传来一声同意。 The government refused to accede to the protesters' demands.
sceneCN: 这里 accede to 指答应诉求（第 1 个义项：同意请求）；句意为政府拒绝答应抗议者的要求。

pos.zh: 同意；应允；就任；加入（条约、组织）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「就任；加入；同意」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「同意；应允」，属罕用词
由 accession 加 -al 构成，义为「与加入或就任相关的」

senses.title: To agree to a request
senses.definition: to say yes to what someone has asked for
senses.definitionCN: 对别人提出的请求表示同意
senses.example: The committee acceded to the request for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会同意了延长时限的请求。
senses.why: Latin accedere meant to go to, and agreeing is pictured as moving over to the other side's position.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accedere 意为「走向」，同意被想象成走到对方的立场那边。

senses.title: To take up a throne or office
senses.definition: to formally begin to hold a throne or a high public office
senses.definitionCN: 正式开始掌握王位或高级公职
senses.example: She acceded to the throne at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十八岁继承王位。
senses.why: To accede to a throne is to move up to it, the spatial sense applied to rank.
senses.whyCN: accede to a throne 就是走向那个座位，是空间义用在等级上。

senses.title: To join a treaty
senses.definition: to become a formal party to an international agreement
senses.definitionCN: 成为一项国际协议的正式缔约方
senses.example: The country acceded to the treaty in two thousand four.
senses.exampleCN: 该国于二零零四年加入该条约。
senses.why: A treaty is a room others have entered; acceding is walking in.
senses.whyCN: 条约是别人已经进入的房间；加入就是走进去。

senses.title: To yield under pressure
senses.definition: to give in to demands after resisting for some time
senses.definitionCN: 抵抗一段时间后向要求让步
senses.example: The minister finally acceded to pressure from the unions.
senses.exampleCN: 部长最终屈服于工会的压力。
senses.why: The movement here is reluctant: the door opens only because pushing has continued.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动作带着不情愿：门之所以开，是因为推了很久。

intro.en: Accede is Latin for going to something, and its senses are all a movement toward a request, a throne, or a treaty.
intro.cn: accede 在拉丁语中意为「走向某物」，它的义项都是朝请求、王位或条约移动。

items.en: Modern English accedes to requests, thrones, treaties, and organisations, always with a sense of formal movement.
items.cn: 现代英语 accede 用于请求、王位、条约与组织，始终带着正式移动的意味。

items.en: Diplomatic writing fixed accession as the technical term for joining a treaty or an international body.
items.cn: 外交文书把 accession 固定为加入条约或国际机构的技术术语。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the verb from French accéder, at first for coming to office and consenting.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 accéder 借入这个动词，最初指就任与同意。

items.en: Accedere joined ad, to, with cedere, to go, giving the plain sense of going toward.
items.cn: accedere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「走」的 cedere 组合起来，字面就是「朝……走去」。

items.en: Cedere, to go or yield, also produced proceed, concede, and recede.
items.cn: cedere「走、让步」还产生了 proceed、concede、recede 等词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same going-toward root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for consenting and yielding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走向」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示同意与让步的动词。

entries.definition: The act of taking office or joining a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就任；加入」。

entries.definition: The act of agreeing or joining, in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，义为「正在同意或加入的」。

entries.definition: The act of assenting; a rare synonym of accession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意；应允」，属罕用词。

entries.definition: The right or ability to enter or use something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权；使用权」，词形与 accede 相近。

entries.definition: To share the same opinion or consent to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意」。

entries.definition: To give permission or approval.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；准许」。

entries.definition: To agree formally to a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式同意」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To give way under pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「屈服；让步」。

entries.definition: To admit or give up something unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认；勉强让步」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin picture of walking toward a door and the formal situations where accede appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「朝门走去」的拉丁画面，以及 accede 出现的正式场合。

normal.en: Ac plus cede: cede means go, so accede is to go toward what is being asked.
normal.cn: ac 加 cede：cede 意为走，所以 accede 就是朝被请求的方向走去。

normal.en: A closed door and a nod inside: the nod is the agreement, the opening is the movement.
normal.cn: 一扇关着的门，里面有人点头：点头是同意，开门是移动。

normal.en: Accede to the throne is the same step, only the chair is higher.
normal.cn: accede to the throne 是同一步，只是椅子更高。

normal.en: Accede to a treaty is walking into a room where other states already stand.
normal.cn: accede to a treaty 就是走进一个别国已经站在里面的房间。

normal.en: Accession is the noun of that step, used in news about kings and unions.
normal.cn: accession 是这一步的名词，见于关于国王与联盟的新闻。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with one door at the end: consent is the walk, not the words.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，尽头有一扇门：同意是那段行走，而不是那些话。

abstract.en: Every sense is that walk: toward a request, a throne, a treaty, a union, or another person's argument.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那段行走：走向请求、王位、条约、联盟，或别人的论证。

abstract.en: The word is formal because the corridor is public, and the step is recorded.
abstract.cn: 这个词之所以正式，是因为走廊是公共的，那一步会被记录。

examples.en: The government refused to accede to the protesters' demands.
examples.cn: 政府拒绝答应抗议者的要求。

examples.en: She acceded to the throne at eighteen.
examples.cn: 她十八岁继承王位。

examples.en: The country acceded to the treaty in two thousand four.
examples.cn: 该国于二零零四年加入该条约。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿西德」——阿西德在门里点了头，门才打开

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ cedere（走、让）→ accedere「走向、靠近」，引申为「同意、就任」。经法语 accéder 进入英语。核心是朝某个位置移动：走向请求、走向王位、走进条约。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses agree to a request, take a throne, join a treaty, and yield under pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项分别是应允请求、即位、加入条约，以及在压力下让步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking toward a closed door and being admitted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人朝关着的门走去，并被允许进入。

branches.en: THE CONSENT: a request is granted.
branches.cn: 应允线：请求被答应。

branches.en: THE THRONE: a ruler takes the seat of power.
branches.cn: 继位线：君主坐上权位。

branches.en: THE TREATY: a state becomes a party to an agreement.
branches.cn: 缔约线：国家成为协定的一方。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE: agreement is given because one is pushed.
branches.cn: 让步线：因为被推着，才表示同意。

branches.en: THE JOINING: consenting and becoming a party are one motion toward an arrangement.
branches.cn: 加入线：应允与成为一方，都是朝同一项安排靠近。

intro.en: Accede is built from a Latin prefix of direction and a verb of going.
intro.cn: accede 由表示方向的拉丁前缀与表示「走」的动词构成。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is cedere, accedere, and accessio; the prefix ad- means toward.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 cedere、accedere 与 accessio；前缀 ad- 意为「朝向」。

items.example: It appears as ac- before c in accede.
items.exampleCN: 在 c 之前它写作 ac-，构成 accede。

items.example: It also gives concede and recede.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 concede 与 recede。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 漂浮的；在海上；不负债的；在流传中
definition_en: floating on water; on a ship or at sea; free of debt and able to continue; in circulation
core_image: 水面托着一样东西：既没有沉下去，也没有靠岸
scene: 渔港的清晨，船身随着潮水轻轻起伏，缆绳在水面投下摇晃的影子。 The old boat stayed afloat through the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 afloat 是「漂浮着的」（第 1 个义项：浮在水面上不沉）；句意为那条旧船在风暴中始终没有沉。画面中可辨识：渔港、起伏的船身、缆绳。

pos.zh: 漂浮的；不负债的；在流传中的
漂浮着；在海上；不欠债地

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（表语形容词）

derivatives.zh: afloat 去掉前缀后的词根动词，义为「漂浮；浮动」，与本词同族
由 float 加 -ing 构成，义为「漂浮的；流动的」，与本词同义场

senses.title: Floating on water
senses.definition: resting on the surface of water without sinking
senses.definitionCN: 停在水面上而没有下沉
senses.example: The old boat stayed afloat through the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧船在风暴中始终没有沉。
senses.why: The prefix a- means on, and float is the verb for resting on water, so afloat is literally 'on float'.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「在……上」，float 是「浮在水面」的动词，所以 afloat 字面就是「处于漂浮之中」。

senses.title: On a ship or at sea
senses.definition: on board a ship or out on the water, especially after leaving port
senses.definitionCN: 在船上或在水上，尤指离港之后
senses.example: The crew spent three months afloat before reaching land.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们在海上待了三个月才靠岸。
senses.why: Once a ship has left land, the whole life on board is literally afloat, so the word came to mean life at sea.
senses.whyCN: 船一旦离岸，船上的整个生活就确实处于漂浮状态，于是这个词也指海上生活。

senses.title: Free of debt and still operating
senses.titleCN: 不负债的；维持得下去的
senses.definition: of a business or person, able to pay debts and keep going
senses.definitionCN: 指企业或个人能偿付债务、继续运转
senses.example: Small grants kept the theatre afloat during the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 小额资助让这家剧院在冬天维持了下来。
senses.why: A business that does not sink is one that stays above its debts, so the water image moved to finance.
senses.whyCN: 没有沉下去的企业就是浮在债务之上的企业，于是水的意象搬到了财务上。

senses.title: In circulation or in the air
senses.definition: of rumours, ideas, or plans, being talked about or circulating
senses.definitionCN: 指谣言、想法或计划正在被谈论、传播
senses.example: There were rumours afloat that the factory would close.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有谣言在流传，说那家工厂要关闭。
senses.why: Words and stories can drift on the surface of a group just as a boat drifts on water.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与故事也能像船漂在水面一样，漂浮在一个群体的表面。

intro.en: Afloat is a native English phrase-word made of a prefix meaning 'on' and a verb for floating.
intro.cn: afloat 是英语本族的短语式合成词，由表示「在……上」的前缀与「漂浮」动词组成。

items.en: Flotian meant 'to float, to rest on water', and it is the direct source of float.
items.cn: flotian 意为「漂浮、浮在水面」，是 float 的直接来源。

items.en: The related noun flota meant 'ship, fleet', showing how early the water image spread.
items.cn: 相关名词 flota 意为「船、船队」，说明这个水的意象很早就扩展了。

items.en: The phrase on flote, literally 'on float', was reduced to the single word afloat.
items.cn: 短语 on flote 字面为「处于漂浮」，后来缩合成单词 afloat。

items.en: Afloat is recorded in the sense of floating on water and of being at sea.
items.cn: afloat 在十六至十七世纪有记录，义为「漂在水上」与「在海上」。

items.en: The financial sense 'out of debt, still operating' developed in modern business writing.
items.cn: 「不欠债、仍能运转」的财务义在现代商业写作中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same float root; the near-meaning group gathers states of floating, drifting, and staying solvent.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 float 词根的一族词；近义组收漂浮、漂流与维持偿付的状态词。

entries.definition: To rest on the surface of water or to move gently through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漂浮；浮动」，是 afloat 的词根动词。

entries.definition: Resting on water or moving freely without being fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂浮的；流动的」，由 float 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Wreckage or goods floating on the sea after a ship has been lost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「漂浮的残骸；漂流物」，与 float 同源，多指海难后的漂浮物。

entries.definition: Able to float or to keep something afloat.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有浮力的；能漂浮的」，侧重浮力而非状态。

entries.definition: Floating without control or direction, often after breaking loose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂泊的；随波逐流的」，强调失去控制与方向。

entries.definition: Having enough money to pay your debts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有偿付能力的」，对应义项三的财务含义。

entries.definition: Spreading among people, as news or rumours do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流传中的」，对应义项四的传播含义。

normalIntro.en: Afloat is held by its simple structure: a- 'on' plus float, and by the business phrase stay afloat.
normalIntro.cn: afloat 可以靠它简单的结构来记：a- 表示「在……上」，加 float；再靠 stay afloat 这个说法固定。

normal.en: A- means on, so afloat is 'on float', resting on the water.
normal.cn: a- 意为「在……上」，所以 afloat 就是「处于漂浮」，停在水面上。

normal.en: Stay afloat is the phrase for a boat that does not sink and a business that does not fail.
normal.cn: stay afloat 既指船不沉，也指企业不倒。

normal.en: Float is the verb, floating is the adjective, and afloat is the state.
normal.cn: float 是动词，floating 是形容词，afloat 是状态。

normal.en: Set afloat can mean launch a ship or spread a rumour.
normal.cn: set afloat 既可指让船下水，也可指让谣言传开。

normal.en: The word has no comparative form because it describes a state, not a degree.
normal.cn: 这个词没有比较级，因为它描述的是状态而不是程度。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf holding its place on a moving river, neither sinking nor reaching the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子在流动的河面上保持位置，既不下沉，也不靠岸。

abstract.en: Think of a shop that pays its bills each month and never quite closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一家每月付清账单、始终没有关门的店铺。

abstract.en: See a rumour as a bottle bobbing on the surface of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 把谣言看成一个在人海表面上下浮动的瓶子。

examples.en: The life jacket kept him afloat until the boat arrived.
examples.cn: 救生衣让他在水面上坚持到船来。

examples.en: The magazine stayed afloat thanks to a few loyal readers.
examples.cn: 多亏几位忠实读者，这本杂志才维持了下来。

examples.en: The harbour lights came on one by one.
examples.cn: 港口的灯一盏接一盏亮了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗洛特」——阿（a）弗（fu）洛（luo）特（te），漂在水面上，不沉也不靠岸。

root: 由 a-「在……上」加 float「漂浮」构成；float 来自古英语 flotian「漂浮」，与 flota「船、船队」同族。

sensesIntro.en: One water state spreads into four: floating, being at sea, staying above debt, and drifting through a crowd as rumour.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种水面状态扩展成四种：漂浮、在海上、浮在债务之上，以及像谣言一样在人堆里漂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held up by water, neither sinking nor landing
core.cn: 核心意象：被水托着的东西，既不下沉也不靠岸

branches.en: The literal state of resting on water.
branches.cn: 停在水面上的字面状态。

branches.en: Life lived on a ship or at sea.
branches.cn: 在船上或海上度过的生活。

branches.en: A business kept above its debts.
branches.cn: 浮在债务之上、仍能运转的企业。

branches.en: Words drifting through a group.
branches.cn: 在人堆里漂流的言辞。

branches.en: Staying on the surface at sea and in finance.
branches.cn: 在海上与在财务上都保持在水面之上。

intro.en: Afloat is a prefix plus a native verb, and its family is mostly forms and derivatives of float.
intro.cn: afloat 是前缀加本族动词，其词族主要是 float 的各种形式与派生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source in this word; the elements are Germanic and the prefix a- is a reduced form of on.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；各成分属于日耳曼语，前缀 a- 是 on 的弱化形式。

definition_zh: （名词）词缀；附加物；（动词）附上；粘贴；盖（印）
definition_en: a letter or letters added to a word to form a new word; to attach or fasten something to a surface
core_image: 一枚被贴上去的小标签：附在词根或物体上
scene: 旧书摊的桌上放着一叠信封，摊主正把一枚邮票按在右上角。 He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 affixed 是「贴上、粘上」（第 3 个义项：把某物固定到另一物表面）；句意为他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。画面中可辨识：旧书摊、信封、邮票。

derivatives.zh: 由 affix 加 -ation 构成，义为「词缀法；附加过程」
由 affix 加 -al 构成，义为「词缀的；与词缀有关的」

senses.title: A word element added to a root
senses.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word to change its meaning or form
senses.definitionCN: 加在词首或词尾、用以改变词义或词形的字母或字母组合
senses.example: The prefix un- is a common affix in English.
senses.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 是英语中常见的词缀。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the physical verb: a prefix or suffix is fastened onto a root just as a label is fastened onto a box.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个物理动词：前缀或后缀就像标签贴到盒子上一样，被固定在词根上。

senses.title: Something attached as an addition
senses.definition: a thing attached or added to something else, often as a minor addition
senses.definitionCN: 附加或添加到另一物上的东西，常指次要的添加物
senses.example: The contract had a short affix listing two extra duties.
senses.exampleCN: 合同后面附了一份简短的附加条款，列出两项额外义务。
senses.why: The noun keeps the literal sense: whatever has been fastened on becomes an affix.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了字面义：凡是被固定上去的东西，就成为一个 affix。

senses.title: To attach or fasten to a surface
senses.definition: to attach, fasten, or stick something onto a surface or object
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附着、固定或粘贴到某个表面或物体上
senses.example: He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。
senses.why: The Latin past participle meant fastened to, and the verb still means exactly that, with no metaphor needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语过去分词意为「固定于」，这个动词至今仍是这个意思，完全不需要比喻。

senses.title: To add a signature or seal
senses.definition: to add a signature, seal, or mark to a document in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上正式加上签名、印章或标记
senses.example: Both parties affixed their seals to the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都在协议上盖了章。
senses.why: A seal is literally pressed onto paper, so this official sense is only the physical act made legal.
senses.whyCN: 印章确实是压在纸上的，所以这个正式义只是把物理动作放进了法律程序。

intro.en: Affix comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to fasten to', and its grammatical sense is a later borrowing of that physical image.
intro.cn: affix 来自拉丁语动词「固定到」，其语法义是后来从这个物理意象借来的。

items.en: Figere meant 'to fasten, fix, drive in', and it also gave English fix.
items.cn: figere 意为「固定、钉入」，它也给了英语 fix 这个词。

items.en: Affigere meant 'to fasten to, attach', built from ad- and figere.
items.cn: affigere 意为「固定到、附上」，由 ad- 与 figere 构成。

items.en: The past participle affixus meant 'fastened to' and became the English noun and adjective stem.
items.cn: 过去分词 affixus 意为「固定于」，成为英语名词与形容词的词干。

items.en: English used affix first for a thing fastened on, then adopted it for word elements in grammar.
items.cn: 英语先用 affix 指被固定上去的东西，后来在语法中用它指词缀。

items.en: Affixation became the standard term for the process of adding prefixes and suffixes.
items.cn: affixation 成为表示添加前缀与后缀这一过程的标准术语。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the same 'fasten' root; the second gathers word-formation and attachment terms.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「固定」词根的一族词；第二组收构词与附着类术语。

entries.definition: The process of adding an affix to a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词缀法；附加过程」，由 affix 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to an affix or to affixes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「词缀的」，由 affix 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To repair something or fasten it in place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修理；固定」，与 affix 同出拉丁语 figere「固定」。

entries.definition: An affix added to the beginning of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词首。

entries.definition: An affix added to the end of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词尾。

entries.definition: Something fastened or joined to another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附着物」，与义项二相近，但更强调连接关系。

normalIntro.en: Affix is best held by the word fix: an affix is something fixed onto something else.
normalIntro.cn: affix 可以靠 fix 这个词来记：affix 就是被固定到别处的东西。

normal.en: Fix means fasten, and af- is the assimilated form of ad-, so affix is to fasten to.
normal.cn: fix 意为「固定」，af- 是 ad- 的同化形式，所以 affix 就是「固定到」。

normal.en: A prefix is an affix at the front and a suffix is an affix at the end.
normal.cn: prefix 是位于词首的 affix，suffix 是位于词尾的 affix。

normal.en: To affix a stamp is the everyday physical use that keeps the original image alive.
normal.cn: affix a stamp「贴邮票」是让原始意象保持鲜活的日常用法。

normal.en: Affixation names the process, and affixal describes anything about affixes.
normal.cn: affixation 指这个过程，affixal 描述与词缀有关的事物。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, while the verb is often unstressed differently.
normal.cn: 名词重音落在第一个音节，动词的读法常常不同。

abstract.en: Picture a small sticker pressed onto the corner of a page, easy to miss but impossible to remove without a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小贴纸压在书页角上，容易忽略，却一撕就会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Think of a word as a body and an affix as a piece of clothing put on at the edge.
abstract.cn: 把一个词想成身体，把词缀想成穿在边缘的一件衣服。

abstract.en: See the same hand that fixes a stamp also fixing meaning onto a root.
abstract.cn: 想象贴邮票的那只手，也在把意义固定到词根上。

examples.en: The affix -ness turns adjectives into nouns.
examples.cn: 词缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

examples.en: Please affix your signature to the bottom of the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。

examples.en: The parcel had no return address on it.
examples.cn: 包裹上没有寄件人的地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲克斯」——阿（a）菲（fei）克（ke）斯（si），把东西固定上去，就像词缀贴在词根上。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 figere「固定」构成 affigere「固定到」，过去分词 affixus 成为英语的 affix；作动词时读「/əˈfɪks/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a physical act of fastening, then splits into the thing fastened on and the grammar term for letters fastened to a root.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初是物理上的「固定」动作，随后分成两条线：被固定上去的东西，以及语法中固定在词根上的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small label pressed onto a surface
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚压在某物表面的小标签

branches.en: Letters fastened to a root to make a new word.
branches.cn: 固定在词根上以构成新词的字母。

branches.en: Any object fastened on as an addition.
branches.cn: 作为附加物固定上去的任何物件。

branches.en: The physical act of sticking something on.
branches.cn: 把某物贴上去的物理动作。

branches.en: A seal or signature pressed onto a document.
branches.cn: 压在文件上的印章或签名。

branches.en: Everyday sticking and formal sealing as one action.
branches.cn: 日常粘贴与正式盖章是同一个动作。

intro.en: Affix is a Latin verb form that became both a noun and a verb in English, with a small but clear family.
intro.cn: affix 是拉丁语动词形式，在英语中同时成为名词与动词，词族不大却清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus figere produced affigere, whose participle affixus English borrowed directly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 figere 构成 affigere，英语直接借用了它的分词形式 affixus。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

definition_zh: 现实；实际情况；真实性
definition_en: the state of being real; what is real as opposed to what is imagined or planned
core_image: 镜头对准一间普通厨房，锅里真的在冒热气
scene: 那位纪录片导演说，他不想要漂亮构图，只想让镜头拍到事情本来的样子。 The documentary maker wanted no beautiful framing; he wanted the camera to catch actuality.
sceneCN: 这里 actuality 指未经修饰的真实状况（第 1 个义项：现实）；句意为导演不要漂亮构图，只想拍到事情本来的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -al 构成，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」
由 actual 加 -ize 构成，义为「实现；使成为现实」

senses.title: Reality as opposed to imagination
senses.definition: the real state of things, especially when it differs from what was expected
senses.definitionCN: 事物的真实状况，尤指与预期不同的时候
senses.example: In actuality, the journey lasted three days.
senses.exampleCN: 实际上，这段旅程持续了三天。
senses.why: The noun names what has been done and exists, which is why it so often corrects a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是已经做成、已经存在的东西，所以它常用来纠正计划。

senses.title: The quality of being real
senses.definition: the degree to which something feels or is genuinely real
senses.definitionCN: 某物在感受上或事实上真正真实的程度
senses.example: The recording gives the scene a strange actuality.
senses.exampleCN: 这段录音给这个场景带来一种奇特的真实感。
senses.why: Beyond the facts themselves, the noun also measures how strongly reality comes through.
senses.whyCN: 除了事实本身，这个名词还衡量现实穿透出来的强度。

intro.en: Actuality is the abstract noun of actual: the state of having been done and therefore being real.
intro.cn: actuality 是 actual 的抽象名词：已经被做成、因而真实存在的状态。

items.en: Agere meant to do, the verb at the root of the whole family.
items.cn: agere 意为「做」，是整个词族根部的动词。

items.en: Actus, a doing, gave the stem act- used by the nouns.
items.cn: actus 表示「一次做」，提供了名词所用的 act- 词干。

items.en: Actualis meant existing in act rather than merely in possibility.
items.cn: actualis 指以行动形式存在，而不只是停留在可能性里。

items.en: English formed the adjective first, and used it for real deeds and facts.
items.cn: 英语先造出形容词，用它指真实的行为与事实。

items.en: The suffix -ity then made actuality, the state or quality of being real.
items.cn: 随后后缀 -ity 造出 actuality，即「真实」这一状态或性质。

note.en: The look-alike group is the actual family; the near-meaning group is the nouns of reality.
note.cn: 形近组是 actual 词族；近义组是表示「现实」的名词。

entries.definition: Real and existing, not imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的；真实的」。

entries.definition: In fact; really.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上；竟然」。

entries.definition: To do something or perform a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行动；表演」。

entries.definition: The world as it really is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实」，最通用。

entries.definition: Something known to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事实」，指可核实的一点。

entries.definition: What is the case, or the quality of being true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「真相；真实性」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep actuality close to the documentary camera and the corrected plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 actuality 拴在纪录片镜头和被纠正的计划旁边。

normal.en: Actuality is actual plus -ity, so it names the state of being real.
normal.cn: actuality 是 actual 加 -ity，命名的是「真实」这一状态。

normal.en: In actuality is the phrase that opens a correction of what people assume.
normal.cn: in actuality 是用来纠正众人假设的那个开头。

normal.en: Radio producers call real recorded sound actuality, as opposed to studio talk.
normal.cn: 广播制作人把现场录下的真实声音称作 actuality，与棚内谈话相对。

normal.en: A scene gains actuality when the background noise is kept, not cleaned away.
normal.cn: 保留背景杂音而不清理掉，一个场景就获得了真实感。

normal.en: Do not confuse actuality with activity: one is reality, the other is doing things.
normal.cn: 别把 actuality 与 activity 混了：一个是现实，一个是活动。

abstract.en: A kitchen with steam on the window and no music added.
abstract.cn: 一间窗上有水汽、没有配乐的厨房。

abstract.en: A tape still carrying the cough of the person who recorded it.
abstract.cn: 一盘还留着录音者咳嗽声的磁带。

abstract.en: A plan lying beside the map that was actually walked.
abstract.cn: 一份计划，和真正走过的地图放在一起。

examples.en: In actuality, the meeting took less than ten minutes.
examples.cn: 实际上，那次会议不到十分钟。

examples.en: The film catches the actuality of a night shift in a hospital.
examples.cn: 这部影片捕捉到了医院夜班的真实状况。

examples.en: She doubted the actuality of everything he described.
examples.cn: 她怀疑他描述的一切是否真实存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克球艾勒提」——阿克把球儿一放，画面立刻变得真实

root: 由英语 actual 加拉丁语抽象名词后缀 -ity 构成；actual 源自拉丁语 actualis「以行动形式存在的」，其根为 agere「做、驱动」的分词 actus；该词十七世纪定型，指真实存在的状态，也用于纪实录音与实况。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the real state of things, and the felt quality of being real.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：事物真实的状况，以及「显得真实」的那种质感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera pointed at an ordinary kitchen where something is really cooking.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜头对准一间普通厨房，锅里真的在冒热气。

branches.en: THE CORRECTION: actuality is what turns out to be the case.
branches.cn: 纠正线：actuality 是最后证实的那个情况。

branches.en: THE TEXTURE: realness can be felt, not only known.
branches.cn: 质感线：真实不只能被知道，也能被感觉到。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a tape keeps the hour as it was lived.
branches.cn: 记录线：磁带把那个小时按原样留住。

branches.en: THE ABSENCE OF POLISH: no music, no lighting gel, no retake.
branches.cn: 未修饰线：没有配乐、没有色纸、没有重来。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: a report of actuality lists what happened.
branches.cn: 文书线：一份 actuality 记录列出真正发生的事。

intro.en: The do-stem act- and two Latin suffixes -al and -ity build the word step by step.
intro.cn: 表示「做」的词干 act- 加上两个拉丁后缀 -al 与 -ity，一步步搭出这个词。

latinIntro.en: Actualis is attested in Latin, and the suffix -itas regularly became English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: actualis 在拉丁语中有文献可证，后缀 -itas 常规律地变为英语 -ity。

items.example: It carries the idea of something done.
items.exampleCN: 它承载「已经做成」的意思。

items.example: It is the base of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由 act 加 -al 构成，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ly 构成，义为「实际上；竟然」

definition_zh: 并排；并肩；不落后；及时了解
definition_en: side by side, level with another, or keeping fully up to date
core_image: 几个人肩并肩排成一条横线，谁也没有超前，谁也没有掉队
scene: 海风很大，三艘小船保持着同一速度，船头排成一条横线。 The two runners stayed abreast for the whole final lap.
sceneCN: 这里 abreast 指两人并排同速前进（第 1 个义项：并排成线）；句意为两名跑者整圈都保持并肩。

pos.zh: 并排地；并肩地；不落后地

derivatives.zh: 同根单纯词，义为「胸部；船的前部」
由 breast 与 bone 合成，义为「胸骨」
由 breast 与 stroke 合成，义为「蛙泳」
由 breast 与 feed 合成，义为「以母乳喂养」

senses.title: Side by side in a line
senses.definition: placed side by side on the same line
senses.definitionCN: 并排放在同一条线上
senses.example: The guards stood abreast at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵并排站在大门旁。
senses.why: A breast is the front of the body, so abreast means front to front along one line.
senses.whyCN: breast 是身体的前部，因此 abreast 就是正面朝前排成一线。

senses.title: Level with a rival in a race
senses.definition: at the same distance in a race, with no one ahead
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中距离相同，没有人领先
senses.example: The two horses ran abreast down the straight.
senses.exampleCN: 两匹马在直道上并排奔驰。
senses.why: Competitors side by side are measured against the same line.
senses.whyCN: 并排的竞争者，是以同一条线为尺度。

senses.title: Keeping up with news
senses.definition: having the latest information about something
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某事的最新信息
senses.example: She reads two papers to keep abreast of the news.
senses.exampleCN: 她读两份报纸以紧跟新闻。
senses.why: To keep abreast is to stay level with events that keep moving forward.
senses.whyCN: keep abreast 就是与不断向前的事件保持齐平。

intro.en: Abreast is a nautical word made from a preposition and a body part, and it has travelled from ships to news.
intro.cn: abreast 是个航海词，由一个介词和一个身体部位词构成，后来从船只走到了新闻。

items.en: In modern usage the phrase keep abreast of dominates, and the physical sense survives mainly at sea.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，keep abreast of 占主导，具体的并排义主要留在海上。

items.en: Newspapers made keeping abreast a matter of reading, not of rowing, and the word entered ordinary prose.
items.cn: 报纸让 keeping abreast 变成阅读的事，而不是划船的事，这个词由此进入日常文章。

items.en: Sixteenth-century sailing accounts use abreast for ships lying side by side on the same line.
items.cn: 十六世纪的航海记述用 abreast 指船只并排处于同一条线上。

items.en: The noun breast meant the front of the body or the front of a ship, the surface that faces forward.
items.cn: 名词 breast 指身体的前部，也指船的前部，即朝前的那一面。

items.en: Old English brēost supplied the body-part noun; the prefix a- comes from on, meaning on or at.
items.cn: 古英语 brēost 提供了这个身体部位名词；前缀 a- 来自 on，意为「在……上」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the body-part noun and its compounds; the near-meaning group collects words for being level or informed.
note.cn: 形近组收身体部位名词及其复合词；近义组收表示「齐平」或「知情」的词。

entries.definition: The front of the body or of a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胸部；船的前部」。

entries.definition: The flat bone in the middle of the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胸骨」。

entries.definition: A swimming style with both arms moving together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛙泳」。

entries.definition: To feed a baby with milk from the breast.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「以母乳喂养」。

entries.definition: Next to and along the side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……旁边；与……并排」。

entries.definition: At the same height or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「齐平的；同水平的」。

entries.definition: Knowing the latest facts about something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「了解情况的」。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「当前的」。

entries.definition: Running side by side at a fixed distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平行的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the nautical picture and the reading phrase that keeps the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用航海的画面，以及让这个词活下来的阅读搭配。

normal.en: A plus breast: two people put their fronts on the same line.
normal.cn: a 加 breast：两个人把胸前的一面朝向同一条线。

normal.en: Ships lying abreast are level, and the phrase keep abreast of news borrows that level line.
normal.cn: 船并排就是齐平，keep abreast of 的消息义借用了这条齐平的线。

normal.en: The opposite of abreast is astern, behind the stern of another ship.
normal.cn: abreast 的反面是 astern，即落在另一艘船的船尾之后。

normal.en: Line abreast is a formation word: the whole row moves as one wall.
normal.cn: line abreast 是队形用语：整排像一堵墙一样移动。

normal.en: When you keep abreast of a field, you walk level with its fastest writers.
normal.cn: 当你 keep abreast of 某个领域，你就与该领域最快的写作者并肩而行。

abstract.en: Picture a row of walkers roped together: the rope is the line, and abreast means no one has slack.
abstract.cn: 想象一排用绳子连着的行走者：绳子就是那条线，abreast 意味着谁都没有松绳。

abstract.en: Cut the rope and the same picture explains news: a fast-moving line of events, and you must stay level with it.
abstract.cn: 把绳子剪断，同一画面也能解释新闻：事件是一条快速移动的线，你必须与它齐平。

abstract.en: Every sense asks one question: are you on the same line, or are you behind?
abstract.cn: 所有义项都在问同一个问题：你是在同一条线上，还是落在了后面？

examples.en: The two boats moved abreast into the harbour.
examples.cn: 两条船并排驶入港口。

examples.en: Readers should keep abreast of new findings.
examples.cn: 读者应当及时了解新的发现。

examples.en: The runners were abreast at the halfway mark.
examples.cn: 跑者们在半程处并排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布瑞斯特」——阿布和瑞斯特并肩走，谁也不肯落后半步

root: 由 a-（on「在……上」）+ breast（古英语 brēost「胸部；船的前部」）构成，字面义为「以胸前一线并排」。十六世纪航海文献用它描写两船同线并行；十九世纪报刊把 keep abreast of 转用于「跟上消息」，遂有「不落后、及时了解」的抽象义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses place things or people side by side, level in a race, and level with the latest news.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把人和物并排放着：并排、比赛中齐平，以及与最新消息齐平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bodies placed front to front on one horizontal line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个身体正面朝前，落在同一条水平线上。

branches.en: THE LINE: two bodies moving side by side.
branches.cn: 并排线：两个身体并着移动。

branches.en: THE RACE: level with a rival.
branches.cn: 竞赛线：与对手齐平。

branches.en: THE NEWS: level with what is happening now.
branches.cn: 消息线：与当下发生的事齐平。

branches.en: THE SIDE BY SIDE: physical alignment is the base of the racing sense.
branches.cn: 并肩线：身体对齐是竞赛义的底子。

branches.en: THE SYNC: keeping up with a neighbour and keeping up with events share one picture.
branches.cn: 同步线：跟上旁边的人与跟上时事，共用一幅画面。

intro.en: Abreast is built from an English prefix and an English noun, so its parts are native rather than borrowed.
intro.cn: abreast 由英语前缀与英语名词构成，构件属本族语而非借词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded for this nautical formation; the parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个航海构词没有拉丁语祖先的记录，其构件来自古英语。

items.example: It appears in aboard and abreast.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 aboard 和 abreast 中。

items.example: It also means the front of a ship.
The recorded form supplies the modern noun.
items.exampleCN: 有记录的形式提供了现代名词。

items.example: It began as a sailing term.
Mothers may breastfeed in this room.
items.exampleCN: 母亲们可以在这个房间哺乳。

derivatives.zh: 胸部；船的前部
胸骨
蛙泳

definition_zh: 断言；肯定；证实；（法律）维持原判
definition_en: to state something firmly as true; to confirm or support a claim; in law, to uphold a judgment
core_image: 把一件事按实、按稳地放在桌上，说「就是这样」
scene: 法庭的木槌还未落下，证人把手放在栏杆上，又重复了一遍自己的说法。 She affirmed that the signature was hers.
sceneCN: 这里 affirmed 是「断言、郑重声明」（第 1 个义项：坚定地声明某事为真）；句意为她断言那个签名是自己的。画面中可辨识：证人席、栏杆、木槌。

pos.zh: 断言；肯定；证实；（法律）维持原判

derivatives.zh: 由 affirm 加 -ation 构成，义为「断言；肯定；确认」
由 affirm 加 -ative 构成，义为「肯定的；赞成的」，也可作名词指肯定回答
由 affirmative 加 -ly 构成，义为「肯定地；赞许地」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「已确认的；被维持的」

senses.title: To state firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to state something firmly and confidently as true
senses.definitionCN: 坚定而自信地声明某事为真
senses.example: She affirmed that the signature was hers.
senses.exampleCN: 她断言那个签名是自己的。
senses.why: Firmus means firm, and affirmare means to make firm, so affirming is planting a statement so it cannot wobble.
senses.whyCN: firmus 意为「稳固」，affirmare 意为「使稳固」，所以 affirm 就是把一句话钉稳，让它不再摇晃。

senses.title: To confirm or ratify
senses.definition: to confirm that something is true or valid, often in an official setting
senses.definitionCN: 确认某事为真或有效，常用于正式场合
senses.example: The committee affirmed the findings of the earlier report.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会确认了早先那份报告的结论。
senses.why: What has been made firm can also be made official: confirmation is the public version of the same act.
senses.whyCN: 被钉稳的东西也可以被正式化：确认就是同一动作的公开版本。

senses.title: To support or defend a value
senses.definition: to express support for a principle, value, or position
senses.definitionCN: 对某项原则、价值或立场表示支持
senses.example: The speech affirmed the importance of free inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲强调了自由探究的重要性。
senses.why: To affirm a value is to hold it firm against doubt, giving it the strength of a stated principle.
senses.whyCN: 肯定一种价值，就是在怀疑面前把它握稳，赋予它一条明确原则的力量。

senses.title: To uphold a court ruling
senses.definition: in law, of a higher court, to declare that a lower court's judgment stands
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，上级法院宣布下级法院的判决继续有效
senses.example: The appeal court affirmed the original verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉法院维持了原判。
senses.why: The judicial sense is the literal one: the ruling is made firm again by a higher authority.
senses.whyCN: 司法义是最字面的：判决被更高一级的权威重新钉稳。

intro.en: Affirm is built on the Latin adjective for 'firm', and its legal sense is close to the original image.
intro.cn: affirm 建立在拉丁语表示「稳固」的形容词上，其法律义最接近原始意象。

items.en: Firmus meant 'firm, strong, steady', and it also gave English firm.
items.cn: firmus 意为「稳固、强壮、坚定」，它也给了英语 firm 这个词。

items.en: Affirmare meant 'to make firm, strengthen, assert', built with ad- and firmus.
items.cn: affirmare 意为「使稳固、加强、断言」，由 ad- 与 firmus 构成。

items.en: Old French passed the verb to English with the sense of asserting or maintaining.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词传给英语，带有「断言、坚持」的意思。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fourteenth century in both statement and legal use.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪已有记录，既用于一般陈述，也用于法律。

items.en: Affirmation and affirmative grew into everyday words for agreement and positive response.
items.cn: affirmation 与 affirmative 发展为日常表示同意与肯定回答的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'firm' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of asserting, confirming, and upholding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「稳固」词根的一族词；近义组收断言、确认与维持类的动词。

entries.definition: A firm statement that something is true, or a positive declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「断言；肯定」，由 affirm 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Expressing agreement or a positive answer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肯定的；赞成的」，也可作名词指肯定回答。

entries.definition: Solid, steady, and not likely to move or change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳固的；坚定的」，是 affirm 所依托的拉丁形容词在英语中的直系形式。

entries.definition: To state something confidently, often without providing proof.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断言；声称」，语气强硬，但不一定给出证据。

entries.definition: To show or state that something is true or correct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实；确认」，强调用证据或权威使某事确定。

entries.definition: To announce something officially or formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布；声明」，侧重公开与正式。

entries.definition: To support a law or decision and declare it still valid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「维持；支持」，与义项四的法律用法最接近。

normalIntro.en: Affirm is remembered through the word firm: to affirm is to make a statement firm.
normalIntro.cn: affirm 可以借 firm 这个词来记：affirm 就是把一句话说得稳稳的。

normal.en: Firmus means firm, and affirmare means to make firm, so affirm is to steady a claim.
normal.cn: firmus 意为「稳固」，affirmare 意为「使稳固」，所以 affirm 就是把主张稳住。

normal.en: Affirmation is the noun, and affirmative is the adjective for a positive answer.
normal.cn: affirmation 是名词，affirmative 是表示肯定回答的形容词。

normal.en: An appeal court affirms a verdict, which means it makes the ruling stand.
normal.cn: 上诉法院 affirm 一项裁决，意思是让判决继续有效。

normal.en: Affirmative action is a fixed phrase about policies that support a group.
normal.cn: 「affirmative action」是表示支持某群体的政策的固定说法。

normal.en: Affirm is stronger than say and more formal than agree.
normal.cn: affirm 比 say 更强，也比 agree 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a sheet of paper flat so the wind cannot lift it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张纸压平，让风无法把它掀起。

abstract.en: Think of a judge's gavel coming down: the sound makes the decision firm.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的木槌落下：那一声让决定变得稳固。

abstract.en: See the word as a nail driven into wood: once in, the claim stays put.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一枚钉进木头的钉子：一旦钉入，主张就不动了。

examples.en: The witness affirmed that she had seen the car leave.
examples.cn: 证人断言自己看见那辆车离开。

examples.en: The court affirmed the earlier ruling on appeal.
examples.cn: 法院在上诉中维持了先前的裁决。

examples.en: The room fell silent as the clerk read the document.
examples.cn: 书记员宣读文件时，房间安静了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿飞尔姆」——阿（a）飞（fei）尔（er）姆（mu），把一句话钉得稳稳的，不让它晃动。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 firmus「稳固」构成 affirmare「使稳固、断言」，古法语传入英语后保留「断言」与「维持判决」两条线。

sensesIntro.en: All senses keep the same image: a statement or decision is made firm, whether by words, by authority, or by a higher court.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都保留同一意象：一句话或一项决定被钉稳，无论靠言辞、靠权威，还是靠上级法院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a claim pressed firmly onto the table
core.cn: 核心意象：把一项主张稳稳压在桌上

branches.en: A statement made firm by the speaker.
branches.cn: 说话人把陈述钉稳。

branches.en: The same firmness given by evidence or authority.
branches.cn: 由证据或权威赋予的同一种稳固。

branches.en: A principle held firm against doubt.
branches.cn: 在怀疑面前握稳的原则。

branches.en: A ruling made firm again by a higher court.
branches.cn: 由上级法院重新钉稳的判决。

branches.en: Confirmation in words and confirmation in law.
branches.cn: 言辞上的确认与法律上的确认。

intro.en: Affirm is a clean Latin prefix-plus-adjective construction, and its family is equally transparent.
intro.cn: affirm 是清晰的拉丁语「前缀加形容词」构词，它的词族同样透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus firmus made affirmare; English kept both the verb and the adjective firm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 firmus 构成 affirmare；英语既保留了动词，也保留了形容词 firm。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.exampleCN: 正在肯定的；正在确认的

latinEntries.example: Firmus is the root of affirm.
latinEntries.exampleCN: firmus 是 affirm 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affirmare passed into Old French and English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affirmare 经由古法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 使苦恼；困扰；使不适；生病
definition_en: to trouble, afflict, or make someone suffer, especially with pain or illness
core_image: 一种说不清的不适，像阴影一样缠住身体或心事
scene: 连续几周，老人吃得很少，也不愿出门。 Something seemed to ail him, though no doctor could name it.
sceneCN: 这里 ail 是「使不适、困扰」（第 1 个义项：使身体或精神感到不适）；句意为似乎有什么在折磨他，可医生都说不出病名。

pos.zh: 动词：使苦恼；困扰；使不适；生病

collocations.zh: 你哪里不舒服；你怎么了

derivatives.zh: 由 ail 加 -ment 构成，义为「小病；不适」
由 ail 加 -ing 构成，义为「生病的；衰弱的；不景气的」

senses.title: To trouble or afflict someone
senses.definition: to cause trouble, worry, or discomfort to a person, often without a clear cause
senses.definitionCN: 给某人带来麻烦、忧虑或不适，常无明显原因
senses.example: Something seemed to ail him, though no doctor could name it.
senses.exampleCN: 似乎有什么在折磨他，可医生都说不出病名。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to weigh on someone: an unseen trouble settles over a person and will not lift.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「压在某人身上」：一种看不见的麻烦罩住一个人，迟迟不肯散去。

senses.title: To be unwell
senses.definition: to be ill or in poor health, used chiefly in literary or older English
senses.definitionCN: 生病或健康不佳，主要用于书面语或较早的英语
senses.example: She has been ailing since the early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她从初春起就一直身体不适。
senses.why: The trouble moves inside the body: the person is no longer the one afflicting, but the one who suffers.
senses.whyCN: 困扰转移到身体内部：人不再是施加折磨的一方，而成了承受折磨的一方。

senses.title: To be the matter with, in questions
senses.titleCN: （疑问句中）使……不舒服；是……的毛病
senses.definition: to be the cause of someone's trouble, used mainly in questions such as what ails you
senses.definitionCN: 成为某人不适的原因，主要用于 what ails you 这类疑问句
senses.example: The nurse asked gently what ailed the child.
senses.exampleCN: 护士轻声问孩子哪里不舒服。
senses.why: A question turns the verb into a search: the speaker asks an unseen trouble to name itself.
senses.whyCN: 疑问句把这个动词变成一次寻找：说话者让那个看不见的麻烦自己报出名字。

senses.title: Archaic: to pain or distress
senses.definition: in older usage, to cause physical pain or emotional distress to someone
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，指给某人造成身体疼痛或情绪痛苦
senses.example: Grief ailed him long after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼过去很久，悲伤仍在折磨他。
senses.why: Before medicine separated body from mind, the same verb could cover a wound and a sorrow alike.
senses.whyCN: 在医学把身体与精神分开之前，同一个动词既能指伤口，也能指悲伤。

intro.en: Ail is a native English verb with Germanic roots, and its older meaning was broader than illness alone.
intro.cn: ail 是带有日耳曼词根的本族英语动词，它较早的含义比「生病」更宽。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meant to trouble or pain, and it left relatives in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个重构动词意为「使烦恼、使痛苦」，在几种日耳曼语言中留下了同源词。

items.en: Old English eglan meant to trouble, plague, or afflict, covering both bodily and mental disturbance.
items.cn: 古英语 eglan 意为「使烦恼、折磨、使痛苦」，兼指身体与精神上的扰动。

items.en: The related adjective egle meant painful or troublesome, showing that the family centred on discomfort.
items.cn: 相关形容词 egle 意为「痛苦的、麻烦的」，说明这个词族围绕「不适」展开。

items.en: In Middle English the verb settled into the form ailen, and illness became its most frequent subject.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个动词定型为 ailen，疾病成为它最常见的对象。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the verb mainly in questions and in the adjective ailing, which also describes weak economies.
items.cn: 现代用法主要把动词保留在疑问句中，并常用形容词 ailing，后者也能形容疲弱的经济。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of troubling and becoming ill.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音相近的词；近义组收表示「困扰」与「生病」的动词。

entries.definition: A noun for a kind of beer, unrelated in meaning to ail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一种啤酒，与 ail 在意义上无关。

entries.definition: A minor illness or disorder, formed from ail with the noun suffix -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ail 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「小病、不适」。

entries.definition: The present participle of ail, used as an adjective for someone or something that is weak.
entries.definitionCN: ail 的现在分词，作形容词指身体衰弱或状况不佳的人或事物。

entries.definition: To cause worry, difficulty, or inconvenience to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人带来忧虑、困难或不便。

entries.definition: To cause suffering or pain to someone over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内给某人造成痛苦或折磨。

entries.definition: To become ill, or to make someone feel ill.
entries.definitionCN: 生病，或使某人感到不适。

normalIntro.en: Ail is a small word for a vague kind of suffering, and these hooks keep that vagueness in view.
normalIntro.cn: ail 是个小词，却指向一种说不清的受苦状态；下面这些钩子让这种模糊感留在眼前。

normal.en: Ail sounds like the sigh at the start of a complaint: a long, low ah.
normal.cn: ail 听起来像抱怨开头的那声叹息：低低的一声「唉」。

normal.en: What ails you is a fixed question, so picture a nurse asking it at a bedside.
normal.cn: what ails you 是固定问法，想象护士在病床边问出这句话。

normal.en: The adjective ailing fits both a sick body and a weak economy.
normal.cn: 形容词 ailing 既能形容生病的身体，也能形容疲弱的经济。

normal.en: Ail is short and dull, much like the tiredness it describes.
normal.cn: ail 又短又沉，正像它所描述的那种疲惫。

normal.en: Link ail with ailment: the noun makes the hidden trouble concrete.
normal.cn: 把 ail 与 ailment 联系起来：名词把隐藏的困扰变成具体的病。

abstract.en: Ail describes trouble that has no clear outline, only a weight.
abstract.cn: ail 描述的是没有清晰轮廓、只有重量的困扰。

abstract.en: The word belongs to the sufferer's side: it names what presses down, not what strikes.
abstract.cn: 这个词站在受苦者一侧：它命名的是压下来的东西，而不是打击本身。

abstract.en: To ail is to be out of order quietly, without drama or a named disease.
abstract.cn: ail 是安静地失去正常状态，没有戏剧性，也没有一个被命名的病。

examples.en: A strange tiredness ailed her all winter.
examples.cn: 一种奇怪的疲惫折磨了她整个冬天。

examples.en: The ailing factory closed two production lines.
examples.cn: 这家不景气的工厂关停了两条生产线。

examples.en: He refused to say what ailed him.
examples.cn: 他不肯说自己哪里不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哎哟」：身体一出问题就忍不住喊「哎哟」，正是 ail 的困扰感。

root: 古英语 eglan（使苦恼、折磨）演变而来，与表示「痛苦」的 egle 同源；核心是缠住人的不适。

sensesIntro.en: Ail covers trouble that weighs on a person, the state of being unwell, the question of what is wrong, and an older sense of plain pain.
sensesIntro.cn: ail 覆盖压在人与上的困扰、身体不适的状态、询问哪里出了毛病，以及较早的单纯痛苦之义。

core.en: A shadow of discomfort settling over body or mind.
core.cn: 一片落在身体或心上的不适阴影。

branches.en: An unseen trouble weighing on a person.
branches.cn: 一种压在某人身上的看不见的困扰。

branches.en: The same trouble turned inward: the person is simply unwell.
branches.cn: 同一种困扰转向内部：人就是身体不适。

branches.en: The trouble becomes a question, asked to discover its name.
branches.cn: 困扰变成一个疑问，用来找出它的名字。

branches.en: The oldest layer: pain or sorrow, before illness was a separate idea.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：疼痛或悲伤，当时疾病还不是独立概念。

branches.en: Both senses keep the trouble hidden and ask someone else to identify it.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让困扰保持隐蔽，要靠别人来辨认它。

intro.en: Ail is a native verb with few affixes, but its -ing and -ment forms do most of the modern work.
intro.cn: ail 是本族动词，词缀不多，现代的用法主要靠 -ing 与 -ment 两种形式承担。

latinIntro.en: Ail has no Latin source; it comes from Old English and Germanic roots, so this section is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: ail 没有拉丁语来源，它来自古英语与日耳曼语词根，因此本节留空。

items.example: Nothing seemed to ail the sturdy old dog.
items.exampleCN: 这只结实的老年似乎什么毛病也没有。

items.meaningCN: 使苦恼；生病（第三人称单数）
items.example: What ails the engine is still unknown.
items.exampleCN: 发动机到底出了什么毛病仍不清楚。

items.example: A mild fever ailed him for two days.

items.meaningCN: 生病的；衰弱的；不景气的
items.example: The ailing bridge was closed to traffic.
items.exampleCN: 这座状况不佳的桥禁止通行。

items.example: A common ailment kept her home.
items.exampleCN: 一场常见的小病让她待在家里。

items.meaningCN: 你哪里不舒服；你怎么了
items.example: The doctor asked what ailed you.
The ailing economy shed thousands of jobs.
items.exampleCN: 疲弱的经济削减了数千个岗位。

items.example: His ailing health forced an early retirement.
items.exampleCN: 他日渐衰弱的健康迫使他提前退休。

items.example: The ailing industry asked for state support.
items.exampleCN: 不景气的行业请求国家支持。

definition_zh: 启动；激活；使活跃起来
definition_en: to switch something on; to make a substance or function start working; to stir people into action
core_image: 一只手指按下开关，原本静止的机器开始转动
scene: 地下车库的灯平时不亮，只有人走近时才会自动通电。 In the underground car park the lights stay off until a sensor activates them.
sceneCN: 这里 activates 指让设备通电开始工作（第 1 个义项：启动）；句意为地下车库的灯在人走近时由传感器启动。

derivatives.zh: 由 activate 加 -ion 构成，义为「启动；激活」
由 activate 加 -or 构成，义为「活化剂；启动装置」
由 de- 加 activate 构成，义为「停用；关闭」

senses.title: To switch a device into operation
senses.definition: to make a machine or system begin to work
senses.definitionCN: 使机器或系统开始运转
senses.example: The sensor activates the light when a car comes near.
senses.exampleCN: 有车靠近时，传感器就会启动这盏灯。
senses.why: The ending -ate turns a state into an action, so act becomes the act of setting something to work.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ate 把状态变成动作，于是「做」变成了「让某物开始做」。

senses.title: To make a substance or function start working
senses.definition: to set a chemical, gene or body function going
senses.definitionCN: 使某种化学物质、基因或身体功能开始发挥作用
senses.example: Enzymes activate the protein once it reaches the gut.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质一到肠道，酶就把它激活。
senses.why: Science needed a word for switching a dormant thing on, and the plain verb of doing was ready.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个词表示「把休眠之物打开」，而那个朴素的「做」正好可用。

senses.title: To stir people into action
senses.definition: to make a person or group begin doing something
senses.definitionCN: 使某个人或群体开始行动起来
senses.example: The campaign activated thousands of young voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动动员了数千名年轻选民。
senses.why: People who were passive begin to do, and they are switched on much as a machine is.
senses.whyCN: 本来被动的人开始做事，他们被打开的方式和机器几乎一样。

intro.en: Activate is English act fitted with a Latin ending that means to make, so it names the moment a dormant thing starts doing.
intro.cn: activate 是英语 act 加上一个意为「使」的拉丁词尾，命名的是休眠之物开始「做」的那一刻。

items.en: Agere meant to do and to drive, and gave Latin its word for action.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动」，为拉丁语提供了「行动」一词。

items.en: Its participle actus, a doing, supplied the stem act- to later languages.
items.cn: 它的分词 actus 表示「一次做」，为后来的语言提供了词干 act-。

items.en: English took act for a deed and for performing, and used it as noun and verb.
items.cn: 英语以 act 表示行为与表演，名词动词两用。

items.en: The ending -atus marked something made or provided with a quality.
items.cn: 词尾 -atus 表示「被造成」或「被赋予某种性质」。

items.en: English verbs in -ate name the act of putting something into that state.
items.cn: 英语中带 -ate 的动词表示「使某物进入那种状态」。

items.en: Technology and biology took activate up for switching devices and chemicals on.
items.cn: 技术与生物学接手 activate，用它表示把设备与化学物质「打开」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the act- stem; the near-meaning group is the verbs of setting things going.
note.cn: 形近组共享 act- 词干；近义组是表示「使某事开始」的动词。

entries.definition: Busy doing things, or producing an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活跃的；起作用的」。

entries.definition: The act of switching something on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「启动；激活」。

entries.definition: To switch something off or make it inactive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停用；关闭」。

entries.definition: To begin operating or to cause to begin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始；发动」，最通用。

entries.definition: To set off a reaction or event suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「触发」，强调突然引起。

entries.definition: To make something possible or usable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使可用；使能够」。

entries.definition: To turn a device on by a switch.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「打开开关」，最口语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the switch: a device, a chemical, and a crowd of people all start doing at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都围着那个开关转：设备、化学物质、一群人，同时开始「做」。

normal.en: Act plus -ate means to put into doing, which is exactly what a switch does.
normal.cn: act 加 -ate 意为「使进入做的状态」，开关做的正是这件事。

normal.en: Phones, alarms and accounts are all activated before they can be used.
normal.cn: 手机、警报与账户都要先 activate 才能使用。

normal.en: In biology an enzyme activates a protein; the protein was there but idle.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，酶 activate 一种蛋白质；那蛋白质本来就在，只是闲着。

normal.en: Activate people means to rouse them from passivity into doing.
normal.cn: activate people 是把人从被动状态唤起来做事。

normal.en: The opposite is deactivate, the prefix de- undoing what was switched on.
normal.cn: 反义是 deactivate，前缀 de- 撤掉先前打开的状态。

abstract.en: A finger pressing a switch and a whole silent room coming awake.
abstract.cn: 一根手指按下开关，整个安静的房间醒了过来。

abstract.en: A sleeping enzyme opening one eye at the touch of the right molecule.
abstract.cn: 沉睡的酶在遇到对的分子时睁开一只眼。

abstract.en: A crowd that was merely standing there suddenly all begin to move.
abstract.cn: 原本只是站着的人群，忽然全都动了起来。

examples.en: Press the red button to activate the alarm.
examples.cn: 按下红色按钮即可启动警报。

examples.en: Sunlight can activate the compound in the glass.
examples.cn: 阳光可以激活玻璃中的那种化合物。

examples.en: A good coach knows how to activate a tired team.
examples.cn: 好教练懂得怎样把一支疲惫的队伍重新带动起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维特」——阿克一按开关，整条生产线都动起来

root: 由英语 act 加拉丁语词尾 -atus（英语作 -ate，表示「使……进入某状态」）构成；act 源自拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」，分词 actus 提供词干 act-；该词在近现代科技语境中定型，用于启动设备、激活物质或动员人群。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one move, switching something from idle to doing: a device, a substance, and a group of people.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个动作——把某物从闲置切换到「做」：一台设备、一种物质、一群人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger on a switch, and the still machine begins to turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按在开关上，静止的机器开始转动。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: current flows and the machine works again.
branches.cn: 设备线：电流一通，机器重新工作。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a sleeping chemical is woken by the right trigger.
branches.cn: 物质线：沉睡的化学物质被对的触发物唤醒。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: passive onlookers are roused into doing.
branches.cn: 人群线：被动的旁观者被唤起而行动。

branches.en: THE SENSOR: the switch may be thrown by a machine rather than a hand.
branches.cn: 传感器线：按下开关的也可能是机器而非人手。

branches.en: THE CHAIN: one activation often sets off the next step.
branches.cn: 连锁线：一次激活常常点燃下一步。

intro.en: The root act- carries the idea of doing, and the suffix -ate adds the idea of making something enter that state.
intro.cn: 词干 act- 承载「做」的意思，后缀 -ate 再加上「使某物进入该状态」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere and actus are attested, and the ending -atus regularly became English -ate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere 与 actus 均有文献可证，词尾 -atus 常规律地变为英语 -ate。

items.exampleCN: 它提供 activate 内部那个「做」。

items.example: It is the ultimate source of act.
items.exampleCN: 它是 act 的最终来源。

definition_zh: 配件；附件；服饰配件；附属物；从犯；附属的；副的
definition_en: an extra item that improves the look or usefulness of something else, or a person who helps another in a crime
core_image: 一件挂在本体旁边的小物件：不改变主体，只让它更完整
scene: 舞台后台的化妆台上摆着几串项链和一条腰带，演员正在挑今晚的搭配。 She chose a silver necklace as the last accessory for her stage costume.
sceneCN: 这里 accessory 指服饰配件（第 2 个义项：首饰、包、腰带等装饰性物件）；句意为她挑了一条银项链作为舞台服装的最后一件配饰。

pos.zh: 名词：配件；附件；服饰配件；从犯
形容词：附属的；附加的；副的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「为……搭配配饰」
由 accessorize 加过去分词词尾构成，义为「配有配饰的」
由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「附属的；附加的」
由 accessorial 加 -ly 构成，义为「附属地；作为附加」

senses.title: An extra piece that completes a thing
senses.definition: a small item added to something larger and more important in order to make it more useful or complete
senses.definitionCN: 附加在更大、更主要的事物上的小物件，用来让它更有用或更完整
senses.example: Every printer in the office comes with a set of accessories.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的每台打印机都配有一套附件。
senses.why: Latin accessorius named something that stands near another thing, so an accessory is literally the item that comes alongside the main one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessorius 指「站在另一物旁边的东西」，因此 accessory 字面上就是陪在主体旁边的那件物品。

senses.title: A fashion item worn for style
senses.definition: a bag, belt, scarf, hat or piece of jewellery that finishes an outfit
senses.definitionCN: 包、腰带、围巾、帽子或首饰，用来完成整体穿着
senses.example: A plain dress can be lifted by a bright accessory at the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 一条素色连衣裙，靠腰间的亮色配饰就能出彩。
senses.why: Clothing is the main body and decoration is what comes beside it, so the old idea of nearness turned into the language of style.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是主体，装饰是陪在旁边的东西，于是「在旁边」这一古老含义变成了时尚领域的说法。

senses.title: An attachment for equipment
senses.definition: a device or part that is attached to a machine to give it an extra function
senses.definitionCN: 加装在机器上、为其增加一项功能的装置或部件
senses.example: The drill kit includes a sanding accessory for wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这套电钻工具包含一个用于木材的打磨附件。
senses.why: The accessory does not replace the machine; it sits beside it and adds a new use, exactly as accessorius described.
senses.whyCN: 附件并不取代机器，而是在旁边为它增加一种用途，这正是 accessorius 所描述的关系。

senses.title: A secondary part of a system
senses.definition: a part that supports a main system without being central to it
senses.definitionCN: 支撑主系统、但本身并不处于核心位置的部件
senses.example: The pump is an accessory unit that feeds the main engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵是为主发动机供料的附属机组。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the word to rank parts: the main unit carries the load, and everything near it is accessory.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了这个词来给部件分级：主机组承担负荷，陪在旁边的都是附属件。

senses.title: A helper in a crime, after the fact
senses.definition: a person who helps an offender escape or hide the evidence after the crime has been committed
senses.definitionCN: 在犯罪已经发生之后帮助罪犯逃脱或隐藏证据的人
senses.example: He was charged as an accessory after the fact for hiding the stolen car.
senses.exampleCN: 他因藏匿被盗车辆而被认定为事后从犯。
senses.why: Law kept the adverb of nearness: someone who stands close to the crime but does not commit it is an accessory.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了「在旁边」这一含义：站在罪行旁边、但并未亲手实施的人，就是从犯。

intro.en: Accessory began as a Latin word for what stands near a main thing, and it now names both a fashion item and a helper in a crime.
intro.cn: accessory 最初是拉丁语中表示「站在主体旁边之物」的词，如今既指时尚配饰，也指罪案中的从犯。

items.en: In current English an accessory is usually a bag, belt or piece of jewellery that finishes an outfit, a sense that grew with department stores.
items.cn: 在现代英语里，accessory 通常指包、腰带或首饰等完成整体造型的物件，这一义项随百货商店的兴起而流行。

items.en: Legal writers fixed the phrases accessory before the fact and accessory after the fact for people who help a crime from outside.
items.cn: 十九世纪的法律作者固定了 accessory before the fact 与 accessory after the fact 两个短语，指从旁协助犯罪的人。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun covered any added item, while the adjective meant additional or subordinate.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词泛指任何附加之物，形容词则意为「附加的」或「从属的」。

items.en: Accessorius was formed from accessor, one who comes near, and described a thing attached to another thing.
items.cn: accessorius 由 accessor「走近的人」构成，用来描述附着于另一物的东西。

items.en: The verb accedere, to come near, joins ad- toward with cedere go, and it is the same root as access.
items.cn: 动词 accedere 意为「走近」，由 ad-「朝向」与 cedere「走」组成，与 access 同根。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same approach root; the near-meaning group gathers words for added pieces and for helpers in a crime.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走近」词根的词；近义组收表示附加物与罪案帮手的词。

entries.definition: A way in, or the right to use something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道；使用权」。

entries.definition: The act of taking office or joining a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就任；加入」，与 accessory 同出 accedere。

entries.definition: To add decorative items to an outfit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为服装搭配配饰」。

entries.definition: Relating to an accessory; supplementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附属的；附加的」。

entries.definition: Able to be reached or used.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的；可使用的」。

entries.definition: An extra part fixed to a machine or device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附加装置；附件」。

entries.definition: Something added to what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增添物；附加部分」。

entries.definition: An additional item that is not essential.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「额外的东西」。

entries.definition: A person who helps another commit a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯；帮凶」。

entries.definition: Added to complete or improve something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「补充的；附加的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a small thing standing beside a larger one.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「小物件站在大物件旁边」这一画面。

normal.en: Access plus ory: the thing that comes near the main object.
normal.cn: access 加 ory：靠近主体放置的那件东西。

normal.en: A phone case is an accessory: the phone works without it, but looks better with it.
normal.cn: 手机壳就是 accessory：没有它手机也能用，但有了它更好看。

normal.en: On a stage the costume is the main act and the necklace is an accessory.
normal.cn: 舞台上戏服是主角，项链只是 accessory。

normal.en: In law the accessory stands beside the principal offender, close but secondary.
normal.cn: 法律上，从犯站在主犯旁边，关系很近，但地位次要。

normal.en: Accessorize is the verb: to add the finishing pieces.
normal.cn: accessorize 是动词，意为「添上点睛的配饰」。

abstract.en: Picture a main body with a small satellite that never leaves its side.
abstract.cn: 想象一个主体，旁边永远跟着一颗小小的卫星。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the idea of nearness: a near item, a near part, a near helper.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留「在旁边」这一核心：旁边的物件、旁边的部件、旁边的帮手。

abstract.en: The legal sense turns nearness into guilt, because helping from the side still counts.
abstract.cn: 法律义项把「在旁边」变成了罪责，因为从旁协助同样算数。

examples.en: She bought a silk scarf as an accessory for her winter coat.
examples.cn: 她买了一条丝巾，作为冬季大衣的配饰。

examples.en: The camera comes with a full set of accessories, including a spare battery.
examples.cn: 这台相机配有一整套附件，其中包括一块备用电池。

examples.en: He was charged as an accessory to the robbery.
examples.cn: 他被指控为这起抢劫案的从犯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞瑟瑞」——阿克在背包侧面塞了个小挂件，只是个配角

root: 拉丁语 accedere「走近」→ accessor「靠近的人」→ accessorius「附属的」→ 英语 accessory。核心是「在旁边」：在衣服旁边的配饰、在机器旁边的附件、在主体旁边的次要部件、在罪行旁边的从犯。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses name an extra part, an item of dress, a device add-on, a subordinate piece, and a person who aids a crime.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项分别指附加部件、服饰配件、设备附加件、附属构件，以及协助犯罪的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small item standing beside a larger one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件小物件站在更大的物件旁边。

branches.en: THE EXTRA: something added to the main thing.
branches.cn: 附件线：加在主物之上的东西。

branches.en: THE DRESS: what completes an outfit.
branches.cn: 服饰线：让一身穿戴完整的东西。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: an add-on for a machine.
branches.cn: 设备线：机器的附加件。

branches.en: THE SUBORDINATE: a part that serves another part.
branches.cn: 附属线：为另一部分服务的部件。

branches.en: THE COMPLICE: a person who helps without doing the act.
branches.cn: 从犯线：不出手却协助的人。

intro.en: Accessory is built from a Latin verb of approach plus a suffix of relation, and it has a regular noun, verb and adjective family.
intro.cn: accessory 由拉丁语「走近」动词加关系后缀构成，并拥有规则的名词、动词与形容词家族。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is accedere, accessor and accessorius.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 accedere、accessor 与 accessorius。

items.exampleCN: 在 c 之前它写作 ac-。

items.example: It supplies the movement in the root.
items.exampleCN: 它提供词根中的运动含义。

items.example: It is the source of access and accessory.
items.exampleCN: 它是 access 与 accessory 的来源。

items.example: It names the person beside the main actor.
items.exampleCN: 它指站在主角旁边的那个人。

items.example: It is the direct source of accessory.
items.exampleCN: 它是 accessory 的直接来源。

items.example: It turns accessor into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把 accessor 变成形容词。

definition_zh: 就任；即位；加入；新增藏品
definition_en: the act of taking up office, joining a treaty, or adding something to a collection
core_image: 一本登记册上写下新名字，把新来者正式记入
scene: 博物馆把新到的画作登记入册，编号写在标签上。 The library announced the accession of a rare manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里 accession 指新藏品入藏（第 5 个义项：新增藏品）；句意为图书馆宣布入藏一份珍本手稿。

pos.zh: 就任；即位；加入；新增藏品

由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与就任或加入相关的」

senses.title: Taking up a throne or office
senses.definition: the act of formally beginning to rule or hold a high office
senses.definitionCN: 正式开始统治或担任高级公职的行为
senses.example: Her accession to the throne was widely reported.
senses.exampleCN: 她继承王位的消息被广泛报道。
senses.why: Latin accedere means to go toward, and taking a throne is moving up to the seat.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accedere 意为「走向」，登上王位就是走向那个座位。

senses.title: Joining a treaty
senses.definition: the formal act by which a state becomes party to an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 一国成为某协议缔约方的正式行为
senses.example: The accession to the treaty took effect in May.
senses.exampleCN: 加入条约于五月生效。
senses.why: A treaty is a room already occupied, and accession is the recorded entry.
senses.whyCN: 条约是一个已经有人的房间，accession 是被记录下来的入场。

senses.title: Joining a union or organisation
senses.definition: the process by which a country joins a political or economic union
senses.definitionCN: 一国加入政治或经济联盟的过程
senses.example: The accession talks lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 入盟谈判持续了四年。
senses.why: The doorway is now a negotiating table, and the word names the whole approach.
senses.whyCN: 门口现在是一张谈判桌，这个词命名的是整段接近的过程。

senses.title: Adding to a collection
senses.definition: the act of adding an item to a library, museum, or archive
senses.definitionCN: 把一件物品加入图书馆、博物馆或档案馆的行为
senses.example: The accession of the archive took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这批档案的入藏花了两年。
senses.why: A collection has a door too: new items are received and written into the register.
senses.whyCN: 收藏也有一道门：新物品被接收，并被写进登记册。

senses.title: An item added to a collection
senses.definition: a single object or document newly added to a collection
senses.definitionCN: 新加入收藏的单件物品或文件
senses.example: The library announced the accession of a rare manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆宣布入藏一份珍本手稿。
senses.why: The act and the object share one noun: what comes in is itself an accession.
senses.whyCN: 行为与物品共用一个名词：进来的东西本身就是一件 accession。

intro.en: Accession is the noun of going toward something, and it now covers thrones, treaties, unions, and museum registers.
intro.cn: accession 是「走向某物」的名词，现在覆盖王位、条约、联盟与博物馆登记册。

items.en: Modern English uses accession for royal succession, treaty entry, union membership, and archive intake.
items.cn: 现代英语用 accession 指王位继承、条约加入、联盟成员资格与档案入藏。

items.en: European integration made accession the standard word for a state joining the union.
items.cn: 欧洲一体化使 accession 成为一国加入联盟的标准说法。

items.en: Museums and libraries adopted accession for the register of newly received objects.
items.cn: 博物馆与图书馆采用 accession 指新收物品的登记。

items.en: Latin accessio meant an approach or an addition, formed from the verb accedere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accessio 意为「接近、增添」，由动词 accedere 构成。

items.en: Accedere joined ad, to, with cedere, to go, giving the picture of walking up to a place.
items.cn: accedere 把表示「朝向」的 ad 与表示「走」的 cedere 组合起来，画面就是走向某处。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same going-toward root; the near-meaning group collects nouns for taking office and adding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走向」词根的词；近义组收表示就任与增添的名词。

entries.definition: To agree, take office, or join a treaty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意；就任；加入」。

entries.definition: A way in or a right to use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道；使用权」。

entries.definition: Able to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的」。

entries.definition: Relating to accession.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与就任或加入相关的」。

entries.definition: The work of registering new collection items.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入藏登记」。

entries.definition: The act of taking on a role or power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就任；承担」。

entries.definition: The act of coming in or joining.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入；加入」。

entries.definition: Something added to a group or collection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增加；新增物」。

entries.definition: The act of becoming part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加入」。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining something new.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获得；收购」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the register and doorway pictures that connect thrones, treaties, and museums.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「登记册与门口」的画面，把王位、条约与博物馆连起来。

normal.en: Accession is accede turned into a noun: the step through the door, written down.
normal.cn: accession 是 accede 的名词形式：穿过门的那一步，被写了下来。

normal.en: A king's accession is a step up; a treaty's accession is a step in; a museum accession is a step onto a shelf.
normal.cn: 国王的 accession 是向上一步；条约的 accession 是向里一步；博物馆的 accession 是上架一步。

normal.en: Accession number is the receipt for that step.
normal.cn: accession number 是那一步的收据。

normal.en: Accession talks are the long corridor before the door.
normal.cn: accession talks 是门前那条长长的走廊。

normal.en: The old sense, formal consent, is still the same movement of the mind.
normal.cn: 较旧的义项「正式同意」，仍是同一种心思的移动。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a desk: every entry is a person or an object that has crossed a threshold.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊开的登记册：每一条记录都是一个跨过门槛的人或物。

abstract.en: Every sense is an entry in that ledger: a reign begun, a treaty signed, a union joined, a manuscript received.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那本登记册里的一条：统治开始、条约签署、联盟加入、手稿入藏。

abstract.en: The word always marks an official beginning, never a private feeling.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终标记一个正式的起点，而不是私人的感受。

examples.en: The library announced the accession of a rare manuscript.
examples.cn: 图书馆宣布入藏一份珍本手稿。

examples.en: Her accession to the throne was widely reported.
examples.cn: 她继承王位的消息被广泛报道。

examples.en: The accession talks lasted four years.
examples.cn: 入盟谈判持续了四年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞申」——阿克的名字被写进登记册，正式入册

root: 拉丁语 accedere「走向」→ 名词 accessio「接近、增添」。经法语进入英语。核心是「跨过门槛并被记录」：君主即位、国家加入条约或联盟、博物馆图书馆入藏新物，皆由这一步而来。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses cover coming to a throne, joining a treaty or body, and adding items to a collection.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项覆盖即位、加入条约或组织，以及为收藏增添藏品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open ledger where each new entry marks a crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊开的登记册，每条新记录都标记一次跨入。

branches.en: THE THRONE: a ruler begins to reign.
branches.cn: 即位线：君主开始在位。

branches.en: THE TREATY: a state becomes a party.
branches.cn: 条约线：国家成为缔约方。

branches.en: THE BODY: a country joins an organisation.
branches.cn: 组织线：国家加入某个组织。

branches.en: THE COLLECTION: a library or museum gains an item.
branches.cn: 收藏线：图书馆或博物馆得到一件藏品。

branches.en: THE JOINING: taking a seat, a treaty or a membership is one motion inward.
branches.cn: 加入线：坐上位置、加入条约或取得成员资格，都是同一个向内靠拢的动作。

intro.en: Accession is a Latin noun of action from the verb to go toward, with a suffix of result.
intro.cn: accession 是一个拉丁行为名词，出自「朝……走去」的动词，带结果后缀。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is cedere, accedere, and accessio.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 cedere、accedere 与 accessio。

items.example: It appears as ac- before c.
items.exampleCN: 在 c 之前它写作 ac-。

items.example: It also gives accede and recede.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 accede 与 recede。

items.example: It is the verb behind accession.
items.exampleCN: 它是 accession 背后的动词。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语名词的直接来源。

与就任或加入相关的
入藏登记

definition_zh: 诚然；无可否认地；据本人承认
definition_en: used to admit that something is true before adding a contrasting point, or in a way acknowledged by everyone
core_image: 说话者先举起一只手，承认对方有理，再继续自己的话
scene: 讨论越拖越久，双方都不肯先松口，会议室里安静下来。 Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it may save money later.
sceneCN: 这里 admittedly 是「诚然、无可否认」（第 1 个义项：先承认某点为真）；句意为诚然这个计划很贵，但以后可能省钱。

pos.zh: 诚然；无可否认地；据本人承认

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「承认；准许进入」
由 admit 加 -sion 构成，义为「承认；准入」
过去分词兼形容词，义为「被承认的；公认的」
由 admit 词干加 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的」

senses.title: Conceding a point before a contrast
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit that a point is true before making a contrasting statement
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，先承认某一点为真，再提出对比性的说法
senses.example: Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it may save money later.
senses.exampleCN: 诚然，这个计划很贵，但以后可能省钱。
senses.why: The adverb marks an admission already made, turning the confession into a stepping stone for argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记一个已经作出的承认，把坦白变成论证的垫脚石。

senses.title: As acknowledged by everyone
senses.definition: in a way that is accepted as true by most people
senses.definitionCN: 以多数人都承认为真的方式
senses.example: The view is admittedly beautiful, even in bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这景色确实美，即使天气不好也一样。
senses.why: Admitted here means accepted, so the adverb simply says the fact is beyond dispute.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 admitted 意为「被接受的」，副词只是说明该事实无可争议。

senses.title: By one's own admission
senses.definition: by the speaker's or the subject's own confession
senses.definitionCN: 根据说话者或当事人自己的承认
senses.example: He is admittedly careless with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他自己也承认在细节上粗心。
senses.why: The word can point back to the person who has already confessed the weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以回指那个已经承认自身缺点的人。

intro.en: Admittedly is simply admitted plus -ly, and admitted is the past participle of admit.
intro.cn: admittedly 就是 admitted 加 -ly，而 admitted 是 admit 的过去分词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, the root behind admit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送」，是 admit 背后的词根。

items.en: Admittere meant to send toward or let in.
items.cn: admittere 意为「朝……送、放进来」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century with the sense of accepting a fact.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪进入英语，带有「接受事实」的意思。

items.en: The past participle came to mean 'acknowledged', as in an admitted fact.
items.cn: 过去分词发展出「被承认的」之意，如 an admitted fact。

items.en: Adding -ly turned the participle into an adverb of concession.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 后，这个分词变成表示让步的副词。

items.en: The adverb settled at the start of a sentence to soften a concession.
items.cn: 这个副词固定在句首，用来缓和让步的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group is the admit family; the near-meaning group gathers other concessive and affirmative adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 admit 这一族词；近义组收其他表示让步或肯定的副词。

entries.definition: To acknowledge a fact or allow entry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认；准许进入」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: The act of admitting or the right to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认；准入」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Allowed to be accepted, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Used to agree strongly or state something as sure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然、确实」，表示强烈同意。

entries.definition: Used to accept a point before arguing, close to admittedly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或连接词，义为「诚然、就算如此」，用法与 admittedly 接近。

entries.definition: Used to confirm or emphasize that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「确实、的确」，用来确认或强调。

entries.definition: By one's own admission, in a formal or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「据承认」，语气正式或偏文学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the adverb out of the participle and its concessive use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从这个分词及其让步用法出发，拼出这个副词。

normal.en: Admitted means acknowledged, so admittedly means in an acknowledged way.
normal.cn: admitted 意为「被承认的」，所以 admittedly 意为「以被承认的方式」。

normal.en: The -ly ending turns the participle into a sentence adverb.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ly 把这个分词变成句子副词。

normal.en: It usually sits first in the clause: admittedly, the cost is high.
normal.cn: 它通常位于句首：诚然，成本很高。

normal.en: It often pairs with but, because it prepares a contrast.
normal.cn: 它常与 but 呼应，因为它是在为对比作铺垫。

normal.en: The same family gives admission and admissible.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 admission 与 admissible。

abstract.en: A hand raised briefly before the argument continues.
abstract.cn: 一只短暂举起的手，然后争论继续。

abstract.en: One stone laid down so the path can go on.
abstract.cn: 先放下一块石头，路才能继续往前。

abstract.en: A door held open for the other side's point.
abstract.cn: 为一方的观点扶住门，让它先通过。

examples.en: Admittedly, the first attempt failed.
examples.cn: 无可否认，第一次尝试失败了。

examples.en: The task is admittedly harder than we expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务确实比我们预想的更难。

examples.en: He is admittedly not the fastest runner.
examples.cn: 他自己也承认不是跑得最快的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米特德利」——阿德先承认，再「得力」地继续争辩

root: 由 admit 的过去分词 admitted 加 -ly 构成。admit 源自拉丁语 admittere「朝……送、放进来」，由 ad- 加 mittere「送」构成；因此 admittedly 的核心是「已被承认地」，用于先让步再转折。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: conceding before a contrast, stating what everyone accepts, and citing the subject's own confession.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：转折前先让步、陈述公认之事、引用当事人自己的承认。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker raises one hand to concede before continuing.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话者先举起一只手表示承认，然后继续说下去。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a point is granted so the main claim can stand.
branches.cn: 论证线：先让出一个点，主论点才站得住。

branches.en: THE CROWD: what everyone accepts needs no dispute.
branches.cn: 众人线：人人都接受的事无需争辩。

branches.en: THE SELF: the subject's own confession supplies the proof.
branches.cn: 本人线：当事人自己的承认提供了证据。

branches.en: THE COMMON GROUND: concession and public agreement both clear the way.
branches.cn: 共识线：让步与公认都在为后续铺路。

branches.en: THE ADMISSION: whether tactical or personal, something is openly granted.
branches.cn: 承认线：无论出于策略还是个人，总有某点被公开让出。

intro.en: Admittedly is a Latin-derived verb plus an English participial ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: admittedly 是一个源自拉丁语的动词，加上英语分词后缀与副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base mittere and its compound admittere are recorded; the English endings are native grammar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础词 mittere 及其复合词 admittere 均有记录，英语后缀则属本土语法。
