definition_zh: 副词；状语词
definition_en: a word that modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb, often showing how, when, or where
core_image: 一个小助手跟在动词身后，调整它的速度与方向
scene: 语法课上，老师把一个句子写在黑板上，圈出修饰动作的词。 In the sentence, the adverb quickly tells us how the action was done.
sceneCN: 这里 adverb 是「副词」（第 1 个义项：修饰动词的词）；句意为在这个句子里，副词 quickly 告诉我们动作是怎样完成的。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「副词的；状语」
由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成，义为「作状语地」
由 adverbial 加 -ize 构成，义为「使副词化」

senses.title: A word that modifies a verb
senses.definition: a word that adds information about how, when, or where an action happens
senses.definitionCN: 补充动作发生方式、时间或地点信息的词
senses.example: In the sentence, the adverb quickly tells us how the action was done.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，副词 quickly 告诉我们动作是怎样完成的。
senses.why: The Latin name means 'added to a verb', so the word is defined by standing beside the verb.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名称意为「加在动词上」，所以这个词是由「站在动词旁边」来定义的。

senses.title: A word that modifies an adjective or another adverb
senses.titleCN: 修饰形容词或其他副词的副词
senses.definition: a word that changes the strength or quality of an adjective or another adverb
senses.definitionCN: 改变形容词或另一个副词的强度或性质的词
senses.example: The adverb very makes the adjective stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 副词 very 让那个形容词的程度更强。
senses.why: The name was extended from verbs to other modifiers, because the same kind of word does the same kind of work.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称从动词扩展到其他修饰语，因为同一类词做着同一类工作。

senses.title: The adverb as a word class
senses.definition: the grammatical category of words that mainly modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs
senses.definitionCN: 主要修饰动词、形容词或其他副词的语法类别
senses.example: Adverbs form one of the traditional parts of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 副词是传统词类之一。
senses.why: Grammar turns the individual word into a class, and the class keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 语法把单个词提升为一个类别，而类别沿用旧名。

senses.title: Any word or phrase doing an adverb's job
senses.definition: loosely, any word or phrase that functions like an adverb in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地说，任何在句中起副词作用的词或短语
senses.example: The phrase after lunch works as an adverb of time.
senses.exampleCN: 短语 after lunch 起时间副词的作用。
senses.why: Function matters more than form, so phrases can be treated as adverbs when they modify the action.
senses.whyCN: 功能比形式更重要，所以修饰动作的短语也可按副词看待。

intro.en: Adverb is a Latin loan translation: a word added to a verb.
intro.cn: adverb 是一个拉丁语仿译词，字面意思是「加在动词上的词」。

items.en: Verbum meant word, and later also verb.
items.cn: verbum 意为「词」，后来也指「动词」。

items.en: Adverbium meant a word added to a verb, modelled on the Greek term epirrhema.
items.cn: adverbium 意为加在动词上的词，是仿照希腊语 epirrhema 构成的。

items.en: Old French carried the grammatical term toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个语法术语带入英语。

items.en: The term is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个术语在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The term widened from words added to verbs to any modifier of a verb, adjective, or adverb.
items.cn: 这个术语从「加在动词上」扩展到修饰动词、形容词或副词的任何词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adverb family and its grammatical neighbours; the near-meaning group names modifier types.
note.cn: 形近组是 adverb 词族及其语法近邻；近义组收各类修饰成分。

entries.definition: Relating to an adverb, or a phrase that acts like one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「副词的；状语」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: In the manner of an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「作状语地」，由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A word expressing an action or state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动词」，是 adverb 这个术语所依附的词类。

entries.definition: A word that describes a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形容词」，与副词同属修饰语词类。

entries.definition: Any word or phrase that limits or describes another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修饰语」，是副词的上位概念。

entries.definition: An adverb that strengthens or weakens another word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强调成分」，如 very、quite 这类副词。

entries.definition: A word that links clauses or sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连接成分」，与句子副词功能相邻。

entries.definition: A short unchanging word with grammatical function.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小品词」，部分副词性小词可归入此类。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal meaning 'added to a verb' and the grammatical family around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面意思「加在动词上」，以及周围的语法词族。

normal.en: Adverb literally means added to a verb, so it is the verb's helper.
normal.cn: adverb 字面意思是「加在动词上」，所以它是动词的助手。

normal.en: The Latin word was modelled on a Greek grammatical term.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁词是仿照一个希腊语法术语构成的。

normal.en: Adverbial is the adjective, and it also names a phrase that behaves like an adverb.
normal.cn: adverbial 是形容词，也指起副词作用的短语。

normal.en: Adverbs answer how, when, where, and how often.
normal.cn: 副词回答「怎样、何时、何地、多久一次」。

normal.en: Many adverbs end in -ly, but not all: fast and soon are adverbs too.
normal.cn: 许多副词以 -ly 结尾，但并非全部：fast 与 soon 也是副词。

abstract.en: A small figure walking beside a larger one, adjusting its pace.
abstract.cn: 一个小人走在大个子旁边，调整着他的步伐。

abstract.en: A dial on a machine that turns the action up or down.
abstract.cn: 机器上的一个旋钮，把动作调大或调小。

abstract.en: A shadow that tells you when and where the action happens.
abstract.cn: 一道影子，告诉你动作在何时何地发生。

examples.en: The adverb slowly describes the way he walked.
examples.cn: 副词 slowly 描述他走路的方式。

examples.en: Adverbs can modify adjectives as well as verbs.
examples.cn: 副词既能修饰动词，也能修饰形容词。

examples.en: Put the adverb before the main verb in this sentence.
examples.cn: 在这个句子里，把副词放在主动词之前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃布」——阿德在动词旁边加了个「沃布」（小助手）

root: 源自拉丁语 adverbium，字面意为「加在动词上的词」，是仿照希腊语 epirrhema 构成的语法术语；由 ad-「向、加于」加 verbum「词、动词」构成。核心是「附着在动词旁边的修饰词」，后来扩展到修饰形容词与其他副词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: modifying a verb, modifying other modifiers, the word class, and any adverbial element.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：修饰动词、修饰其他修饰语、副词词类，以及任何状语性成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small helper walks beside a verb and adjusts its speed and direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小助手走在动词旁边，调整它的速度与方向。

branches.en: THE VERB: the helper tells how the action happens.
branches.cn: 动词线：助手说明动作怎样发生。

branches.en: THE OTHER MODIFIER: the same helper strengthens an adjective or another adverb.
branches.cn: 其他修饰语线：同一助手加强形容词或另一个副词。

branches.en: THE CLASS: grammar gathers all such words under one name.
branches.cn: 词类线：语法把所有这类词归入一个名称。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: a phrase can do the same job as one word.
branches.cn: 功能线：短语也能完成单词同样的工作。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTMENT: whether beside a verb or adjective, the role is to modify.
branches.cn: 调整线：无论跟在动词还是形容词旁，角色都是修饰。

intro.en: Adverb is a Latin compound of 'to' and 'word', used as a grammatical label.
intro.cn: adverb 是拉丁语「向」与「词」的复合词，用作语法标签。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbum and adverbium are recorded; the Greek model epirrhema is also attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verbum 与 adverbium 均有记录，希腊语范本 epirrhema 也有文献。

items.example: It marks the word as added to another.
items.exampleCN: 它标出这个词是加在另一个词上的。

items.example: It is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是复合词的后半部分。

items.example: It is the direct source of adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adverb 的直接来源。

items.example: It was the model for the Latin term.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个拉丁术语的范本。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「副词的；状语」
由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成，义为「作状语地」
由 adverbial 加 -ize 构成，义为「使副词化」

definition_zh: 赞誉；喝彩；公开称赞；拥立；好评
definition_en: to praise someone or something publicly and with enthusiasm, or the loud approval that such praise produces
core_image: 一群人仰起头，朝台上的人大声喊出肯定
scene: 首映结束，灯光亮起，观众站成一排鼓掌，影评人也在低声议论。 The director was acclaimed for a film that had taken ten years to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 acclaim 指公开称赞（第 1 个义项：公开赞扬某人或其作品）；句意为这位导演因一部耗时十年的影片受到赞誉。

pos.zh: 动词：公开称赞；欢呼拥立

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「广受赞誉的」
由拉丁语 acclamatio 借入，义为「欢呼；喝彩；鼓掌通过」
由 acclamation 加 -ory 构成，义为「表示欢呼的」

senses.title: To praise publicly
senses.definition: to praise a person, work or action openly and with strong approval
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地赞许某人、某作品或某行为
senses.example: Reviewers acclaimed the novel as a masterpiece.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者称赞这部小说是杰作。
senses.why: Latin acclamare meant to shout toward someone, so praise begins as a loud voice aimed at the person on stage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acclamare 意为「朝某人喊叫」，所以称赞最初是朝台上之人发出的响亮声音。

senses.title: To declare someone something
senses.definition: to declare a person to be a king, leader or winner by general agreement
senses.definitionCN: 以众人一致的方式宣布某人为国王、领袖或获胜者
senses.example: The crowd acclaimed him captain after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，人群拥立他为队长。
senses.why: A shout can do more than praise: when enough voices agree, the shout turns into an official declaration.
senses.whyCN: 喊声不止是称赞：当足够多的声音一致时，喊声就变成了正式的宣布。

senses.title: Loud applause from an audience
senses.definition: the noise of cheers and clapping that a crowd makes to show approval
senses.definitionCN: 人群为表示赞许而发出的欢呼与掌声
senses.example: The singer stepped out to the acclaim of the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手在全场掌声中走上舞台。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical sound: approval measured in decibels rather than in printed words.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了物理的声音：赞许以分贝来衡量，而不是以文字来衡量。

senses.title: Praise from critics
senses.definition: approval expressed by reviewers and experts, especially for a film, book or play
senses.definitionCN: 影评人、书评人等专业人士表达的赞许，尤指对电影、书或戏剧
senses.example: Her first collection earned critical acclaim but sold few copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部诗集获得了评论界的好评，但销量很少。
senses.why: Modern culture separated the loud crowd from the quiet reviewer, and acclaim now covers both kinds of approval.
senses.whyCN: 现代文化把喧闹的人群与安静的评论者分开，而 acclaim 现在同时覆盖这两种赞许。

intro.en: Acclaim is a Latin shout turned into praise. It first named the noise of welcome and later grew into the language of reviews and reputations.
intro.cn: acclaim 是一个由「喊叫」变成「称赞」的拉丁词。它最初指欢迎的声响，后来发展成评论与声誉的语言。

items.en: Film festivals and review pages made critical acclaim a standard phrase, and an acclaimed actor is one whose work has been praised.
items.cn: 电影节与评论版面使 critical acclaim 成为固定说法，而 acclaimed 演员指的是作品受到称赞的演员。

items.en: The phrase by popular acclaim recorded appointments made by a crowd rather than by a formal ballot.
items.cn: 短语 by popular acclaim 记录了靠人群而非正式投票作出的任命。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the verb meant both to shout in welcome and to declare someone a ruler.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个动词既表示欢呼迎接，也表示宣布某人为统治者。

items.en: Acclamare joined ad- toward with clamare to shout, and described a cry directed at a person.
items.cn: acclamare 由 ad-「朝向」与 clamare「喊叫」组成，描述朝某人发出的呼喊。

items.en: Clamare, to cry out, also gave English exclaim, claim and clamour, all built on the same loud voice.
items.cn: clamare 意为「大声喊」，还产生了英语的 exclaim、claim 与 clamour，它们都建立在同一个「响亮的声音」上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the shout root; the near-meaning group gathers words for praise and applause.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「喊叫」词根的词；近义组收表示称赞与鼓掌的词。

entries.definition: Loud and enthusiastic approval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「欢呼；喝彩；鼓掌通过」。

entries.definition: Expressing cheers or approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「表示欢呼的」。

entries.definition: Widely praised, especially by critics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广受赞誉的」。

entries.definition: To cry out suddenly because of strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼喊；惊叫」，与 acclaim 同出 clamare。

entries.definition: A loud and confused noise of many voices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喧嚷；吵闹」，同出 clamare。

entries.definition: To express approval or admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「称赞；赞扬」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: To clap the hands to show approval.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓掌」，侧面对现场的动作。

entries.definition: To praise formally or officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表扬；嘉许」，语气偏正式。

entries.definition: To greet or describe as great.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼致意；称颂」，带公开宣告色彩。

entries.definition: To shout in encouragement or joy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欢呼；喝彩」，强调声音而非评价。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a crowd shouting approval at someone standing above them.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「人群朝站在高处的人大声喊出赞许」这一画面。

normal.en: Acclaim sounds like a claim shouted out: the crowd claims that this person is great.
normal.cn: acclaim 听起来像被喊出来的 claim：人群宣称这个人了不起。

normal.en: Picture the exclamation mark above a theatre: the louder the praise, the higher the mark.
normal.cn: 想象剧院上方有一个感叹号：赞许喊得越响，符号就立得越高。

normal.en: Critical acclaim is praise written down; popular acclaim is praise shouted out.
normal.cn: critical acclaim 是写下来的赞许，popular acclaim 是喊出来的赞许。

normal.en: An acclaimed film is one that the crowd has already shouted about.
normal.cn: acclaimed 影片指的是人群已经为之呼喊过的影片。

normal.en: By popular acclaim means the crowd itself did the voting with its voice.
normal.cn: by popular acclaim 意为人群用声音完成了投票。

abstract.en: Picture a single voice starting in the back row and the whole hall joining in.
abstract.cn: 想象后排的一个声音先起，随后整个大厅跟着一起喊。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a public sound: praise is never silent.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留一种公开的声音：赞许从来不是沉默的。

abstract.en: The noun turns the sound into a reputation that travels beyond the hall.
abstract.cn: 名词把声音变成一种能传出大厅之外的声誉。

examples.en: The film won critical acclaim at the festival.
examples.cn: 这部影片在电影节上获得评论界的好评。

examples.en: Critics acclaimed her performance as the best of the year.
examples.cn: 评论者称赞她的演出是当年最佳。

examples.en: The crowd acclaimed the returning champion with cheers.
examples.cn: 人群以欢呼迎接归来的冠军。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄克莱姆」——台下的人一声接一声地喊，把掌声送到台上

root: 拉丁语 acclamare「朝……呼喊」← ad-「朝向」+ clamare「喊叫」→ 英语 acclaim。核心是「朝人喊出肯定」：公开称赞、拥护称王、现场掌声、评论界好评、公众声誉、以呼声推举。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses cover public praise, a shout that hails someone, the noise of a crowd, and the verdict of critics.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项覆盖公开称赞、以呼声拥立、人群的声浪，以及评论界的评价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd shouting approval at someone on stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群朝台上的某人大声喊出赞许。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: approval spoken aloud.
branches.cn: 称赞线：说出口的赞许。

branches.en: THE HAIL: a crowd calls a person to honour.
branches.cn: 拥立线：人群呼喊以示尊崇。

branches.en: THE NOISE: applause and cheers in a hall.
branches.cn: 声浪线：厅堂里的掌声与欢呼。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: reviewers agree on worth.
branches.cn: 评论线：评论者一致认定其价值。

branches.en: THE VOICE: spoken praise and crowd noise are one sound at different volumes.
branches.cn: 声线：口头称赞与人群声浪，是同一种声音的不同音量。

intro.en: Acclaim is a Latin verb of shouting with a directional prefix, and its noun and adjective forms follow regular patterns.
intro.cn: acclaim 是一个带方向前缀的拉丁「喊叫」动词，其名词与形容词形式遵循规则模式。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is clamare, acclamare and acclamatio.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 clamare、acclamare 与 acclamatio。

items.example: It appears as ac- before c.
items.exampleCN: 在 c 之前它写作 ac-。

items.example: It also gives exclaim and clamour.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 exclaim 与 clamour。

items.example: It is the direct source of acclaim.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acclaim 的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: 欢呼；喝彩；鼓掌通过
广受赞誉的
表示欢呼的

definition_zh: 使人上瘾的；令人着迷的
definition_en: causing a person to become dependent on a substance or activity; so engaging that people want more and more
core_image: 一局结束，手指已经自动点了「再来一局」
scene: 那款小游戏规则简单，赢一把就想再赢一把，不少人说它格外让人上瘾。 The little game had simple rules, and one win made players want another; many called it unusually addictive.
sceneCN: 这里 addictive 指让人上瘾、停不下来（第 1 个义项：使人上瘾的）；句意为一赢就想再赢，玩家觉得它特别容易让人沉迷。

pos.zh: 使人上瘾的；令人着迷的

derivatives.zh: 由 addictive 加 -ly 构成，义为「让人上瘾地」
由 addictive 加 -ness 构成，义为「成瘾性」
由同一词干构成，义为「成瘾者」
由 addict 加 -ion 构成，义为「成瘾」

senses.title: Causing real dependence
senses.definition: causing the body or mind to need a substance or activity more and more
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或心理对某种物质或活动越来越离不开
senses.example: Nicotine is one of the most addictive substances known.
senses.exampleCN: 尼古丁是已知最容易让人上瘾的物质之一。
senses.why: The adjective describes the power a thing has over the person who uses it, not the person's own weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述的是某物对使用者施加的力量，而不是使用者本人的软弱。

senses.title: Hard to stop for pleasure alone
senses.definition: so engaging that people find it hard to stop, even when there is no physical dependence
senses.definitionCN: 极其吸引人，即使没有生理依赖也让人难以停下
senses.example: The show is addictive in the way a good puzzle is.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧像一道好谜题那样让人停不下来。
senses.why: The same word stretches from drugs to pleasure, because the pull feels similar from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从药物延伸到娱乐，因为从内心感受来说，那股拉力很像。

intro.en: addictive is a young adjective built on an old legal word; the ending -ive turned the act of handing someone over into a quality of the thing that does it.
intro.cn: addictive 是个年轻的形容词，长在一个古老的法律词上；词尾 -ive 把「把人交出去」的动作变成施事物的一种性质。

items.en: Addicere meant to assign, and its participle described a person handed over.
items.cn: addicere 意为判归，其分词描述被交付出去的人。

items.en: Addictus named the person bound over, not the thing that bound them.
items.cn: addictus 指被绑过去的人，而不是绑住他们的东西。

items.en: English used addict for someone given over to a practice or passion.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 addict 指把自己交给某种做法或激情的人。

items.en: Medical writing began to speak of drugs that create dependence.
items.cn: 医学写作开始谈论会制造依赖的药物。

items.en: The adjective widened again, so games and shows could be called addictive.
items.cn: 这个形容词再次扩展，游戏和节目也能被称作 addictive。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family at different distances; the near-meaning group is other adjectives of strong pull.
note.cn: 形近组是同一家族在不同距离上的成员；近义组是其他表示「强拉力」的形容词。

entries.definition: Unable to stop using a substance or habit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上瘾的」，说的是人。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to stop.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾」，说的是状态。

entries.definition: A person held by a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成瘾者」，说的是人。

entries.definition: Tending to create a habit that is hard to break.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「容易成瘾的」，语气较中性。

entries.definition: So interesting that attention cannot easily leave it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人入胜的」，只指吸引力。

entries.definition: Pleasant and interesting enough to hold attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迷人的、有趣的」，不含成瘾义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks separate the medical sense from the everyday sense of a pleasure that will not let go.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把医学上的成瘾与日常里「快乐抓人」的用法分开。

normal.en: The ending -ive means tending to, so addictive is the quality of tending to create addicts.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 意为「有…倾向」，所以 addictive 就是「倾向于制造成瘾者」的性质。

normal.en: The word began with drugs and later spread to games, shows and apps.
normal.cn: 这个词从药物开始，后来扩展到游戏、节目和应用。

normal.en: Addicted describes the person; addictive describes the thing.
normal.cn: addicted 描述人，addictive 描述物。

normal.en: A substance is addictive because stopping it produces real withdrawal.
normal.cn: 一种物质之所以 addictive，是因为停用它会产生真实的戒断反应。

normal.en: A game can be addictive without any chemical at all, because the pull is psychological.
normal.cn: 游戏完全不含化学成分也能让人上瘾，因为那股拉力是心理上的。

abstract.en: A finger tapping the same button without a decision.
abstract.cn: 手指没有经过决定就点了同一个按钮。

abstract.en: One more episode at the edge of midnight.
abstract.cn: 午夜边缘的「再看一集」。

abstract.en: A craving that arrives before the thought of it.
abstract.cn: 渴望先到，念头后到。

examples.en: The game is addictive but harmless.
examples.cn: 这款游戏让人上瘾，但并无害处。

examples.en: Doctors warn that these pills can be addictive.
examples.cn: 医生警告说这些药片可能让人成瘾。

examples.en: Addictive habits are easier to start than to break.
examples.cn: 让人上瘾的习惯，开始容易，戒掉很难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱得克缇芙」——爱得太深，身体被它克住，怎么也停不下来

root: 由 addict 加形容词词尾 -ive 构成；addict 出自拉丁语 addicere「判归、交付」的过去分词 addictus。十九世纪医学开始用这个词族描述制造依赖的药物，现代又扩展到游戏、节目等一切让人停不下来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: one about chemical or behavioural dependence, one about a pleasure that will not release its hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：一个指生理或行为上的依赖，一个指让人无法松手的娱乐吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger already pressing the same button again.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指已经又一次按下同一个按钮。

branches.en: THE DRUG: the substance creates a growing need.
branches.cn: 药物线：物质制造出越来越大的需求。

branches.en: THE DOSE: more is required for the same effect.
branches.cn: 剂量线：要达到同样的效果，需要更多。

branches.en: THE GAME: pleasure alone can hold attention.
branches.cn: 游戏线：单靠乐趣就能抓住注意力。

branches.en: THE SHOW: one episode leads straight into the next.
branches.cn: 剧集线：一集结束，直接接上下一集。

branches.en: THE PULL: in both cases stopping feels like a loss.
branches.cn: 拉力线：在两种情况下，停下来都像是一种损失。

intro.en: A Latin participle meaning handed over took the English ending -ive, which turns a base into a quality that acts on someone.
intro.cn: 一个意为「被交付」的拉丁分词接上英语词尾 -ive，把词基变成一种作用在人身上的性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin parts belong to the addict family; -ive and the other endings are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁部件属于 addict 这一族；-ive 等词尾是英语后加的。

items.example: It points the assigning towards the person.
It supplies the declaring element of addicere.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 addicere 中「宣布」的成分。

items.example: It is the stem behind the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个英语词族背后的词干。

items.example: It turns the act of addicting into the quality addictive.
items.exampleCN: 它把「使人成瘾」这个动作变成性质 addictive。

items.example: It is the base to which -ive is attached.

derivatives.zh: 由 addictive 加 -ly 构成，义为「让人上瘾地」
由 addictive 加 -ness 构成，义为「成瘾性」
同词干名词，义为「成瘾者」
由 addict 加 -ion 构成，义为「成瘾」

definition_zh: 极度痛苦；苦恼；（临死前的）挣扎
definition_en: extreme physical or mental pain, or the final struggle before death
core_image: 一个人蜷缩在地，痛得说不出话
scene: 急诊室外，伤者的家属抱头蹲在走廊里。 The agony on his face silenced everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 agony 是「极度痛苦」（第 1 个义项：身体上剧烈的疼痛）；句意为他脸上的痛苦让屋里所有人都沉默了。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊、病床、家属。

pos.zh: 名词：极度痛苦；苦恼；临死挣扎

collocations.zh: 知心姐姐；答读者问专栏作家

derivatives.zh: 由 agon 加 -ize 构成，义为「使极度痛苦；苦苦思索」
由 agonize 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人极度痛苦的」
由 agonize 加 -ed 构成，义为「痛苦的；显得痛苦的」

senses.title: Extreme physical pain
senses.definition: very severe pain in the body, such as that of a serious injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上极为剧烈的疼痛，如重伤或重病所带来的
senses.example: The agony on his face silenced everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上的痛苦让屋里所有人都沉默了。
senses.why: Greek agōn was a contest or struggle; agony is the body fighting a losing battle against pain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 agōn 指「竞赛、搏斗」；agony 就是身体在与疼痛打一场必败的仗。

senses.title: Mental torment
senses.definition: very great emotional suffering, especially while waiting or fearing something
senses.definitionCN: 极度的情感痛苦，尤见于等待或恐惧某事之时
senses.example: She endured the agony of waiting for the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍受着等待检查结果的精神折磨。
senses.why: The struggle can be fought in the mind alone; no wound is needed for the word to apply.
senses.whyCN: 这场搏斗也能只在心里进行；不需要伤口，这个词同样适用。

senses.title: The struggle before death
senses.definition: the violent final struggle of a dying person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物临死时剧烈的最后挣扎
senses.example: The wounded bird lay in its death agony.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的鸟在临死的挣扎中躺着。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical sense: life itself is the contest being lost.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最身体化的义项：生命本身成了那场输掉的搏斗。

senses.title: A painful ordeal
senses.definition: an experience that is extremely difficult or unpleasant to go through
senses.definitionCN: 一段极其艰难或令人难受的经历
senses.example: The final exam was agony from the first minute.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试从第一分钟起就是煎熬。
senses.why: Everyday speech stretches the word from a wound to any experience that feels like one.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把这个词从伤口延伸到任何感觉像伤口的经历。

senses.title: A hard final effort
senses.definition: an intense, exhausting struggle or effort, especially at the end of something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而耗竭的挣扎或努力，尤指某事接近尾声时
senses.example: The last kilometer of the race was pure agony.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛最后一公里纯粹是苦撑。
senses.why: Any contest has its last stretch, where effort becomes pain; the word names that stretch.
senses.whyCN: 任何竞赛都有最后一段，努力在那里变成疼痛；这个词就指那一段。

intro.en: Agony comes from the Greek word for a contest, then for the struggle of the dying.
intro.cn: agony 出自希腊语表示「竞赛」的词，随后指临死时的挣扎。

items.en: Agōn meant an athletic contest, a struggle, or a trial, with the sense of a fight for victory.
items.cn: agōn 意为「竞技、搏斗、考验」，带有为胜利而战的意思。

items.en: Agōnia named the struggle itself, especially the last struggle of a dying person.
items.cn: agōnia 指搏斗本身，尤指临死之人的最后挣扎。

items.en: Latin borrowed agōnia with the same sense of severe pain or death struggle.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 agōnia，仍指剧痛或临死的挣扎。

items.en: English took the word through French and used it first for the pain of dying.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入这个词，最初用于指死亡的痛苦。

items.en: The sense widened to any extreme pain, mental or physical, and to painful experiences.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何极度的身心痛苦，以及令人难受的经历。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root verbs and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for severe suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收同根动词与形容词；近义组收表示剧烈痛苦的词。

entries.definition: To suffer or cause great pain, or to struggle painfully with a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「极度痛苦；苦苦思索」，也指使人痛苦。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning causing extreme pain or anxiety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人极度痛苦的；令人焦虑的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a face or cry that shows great pain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「痛苦的」，形容显出极大痛苦的面容或叫声。

entries.definition: A feeling of physical hurt caused by injury or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疼痛」，指伤病引起的身体痛感。

entries.definition: Great suffering of the mind, often caused deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折磨；煎熬」，多指精神上被施加的痛苦。

entries.definition: The state of experiencing pain, illness, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苦难；痛苦」，指经历疼痛、疾病或艰难的境况。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to Greek contests, doomed struggles and the look of a face in pain.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与希腊竞赛、必败的挣扎以及痛苦的面容联系起来。

normal.en: AGONY begins with agon, the Greek word for a contest.
normal.cn: agony 开头是 agon，希腊语指「竞赛」。

normal.en: Picture a runner who has lost the final and cannot stand up.
normal.cn: 想象一名输掉决赛、站不起来的赛跑者。

normal.en: The ending -y turns the struggle into a state you are in.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把搏斗变成一个你所处的状态。

normal.en: Agony and agonize share the same ache, one as a noun and one as a verb.
normal.cn: agony 与 agonize 共享同一种疼痛，一个作名词，一个作动词。

normal.en: A long queue at the dentist is a familiar picture of agony.
normal.cn: 牙医诊所前的长队是常见的「煎熬」画面。

abstract.en: Agony is a battle with no enemy but pain itself.
abstract.cn: 极度痛苦是一场没有敌人、只有疼痛本身的仗。

abstract.en: The Greeks saw life as a contest, and the word kept that vision.
abstract.cn: 希腊人把生命看作竞赛，这个词保留了这个图景。

abstract.en: Waiting often hurts more than the news being waited for.
abstract.cn: 等待往往比等到的消息更折磨人。

examples.en: He fell to his knees in agony.
examples.cn: 他痛苦地跪倒在地。

examples.en: The agony of not knowing lasted for weeks.
examples.cn: 不知结果的煎熬持续了数周。

examples.en: She described the climb as hours of agony.
examples.cn: 她把那次攀登形容为长达数小时的苦撑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啊，哥你」：啊，哥你疼得脸都变形了，真是极度的痛苦。

root: 希腊语 agōn（竞赛、搏斗）生出 agōnia（挣扎、临死的痛苦），经拉丁语与法语进入英语，核心是「与疼痛进行一场搏斗」。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from bodily torment to mental anguish, the death struggle, painful ordeals and the final exhausting effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从身体的剧痛走到精神的折磨、临死的挣扎、难熬的经历以及最后耗尽气力的苦撑。

core.en: A STRUGGLE AGAINST PAIN
core.cn: 与疼痛的搏斗

branches.en: the body fighting severe pain
branches.cn: 身体与剧痛搏斗

branches.en: the mind fighting fear and waiting
branches.cn: 心与恐惧和等待搏斗

branches.en: life losing its final contest
branches.cn: 生命输掉最后一场搏斗

branches.en: an experience felt as pain
branches.cn: 被感受为疼痛的经历

branches.en: the last stretch of a hard effort
branches.cn: 艰苦努力的最后一段

intro.en: Agony sits on the Greek root agon 'contest', which also shapes agonize and antagonist.
intro.cn: agony 立在希腊词根 agon「竞赛」上，agonize 与 antagonist 也由此而来。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek rather than Latin; it entered English through Latin and French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，经由拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。

items.meaning: to suffer or cause extreme pain, or struggle over a choice
items.example: He agonized over the letter for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他为一封信苦苦纠结了一个小时。

items.example: It was an agonizing wait for news.
items.exampleCN: 那是对消息的煎熬等待。

items.example: She let out an agonized cry.
items.exampleCN: 她发出一声痛苦的喊叫。

items.meaning: in a painfully slow or painful way
items.meaningCN: 令人痛苦地；极其缓慢地
items.exampleCN: 那几分钟过去得慢得令人痛苦。

items.meaning: a columnist who gives advice to readers
items.meaningCN: 知心姐姐；答读者问专栏作家
items.example: The agony aunt answered three letters that week.
items.exampleCN: 那位知心姐姐那周回了三封信。

items.meaning: a newspaper feature of readers' problems and advice
items.example: He found the advice in the agony column.
items.exampleCN: 他在读者问答专栏里找到了建议。

items.example: The word agon survives mainly in compounds.
items.exampleCN: agon 主要保留在复合词中。

items.meaning: to make someone hostile or opposed

definition_zh: 针灸；针刺疗法
definition_en: a medical practice of inserting thin needles at points on the body; the insertion of such needles
core_image: 几根细如发丝的银针稳稳立在皮肤上，病人的肩慢慢松下来
scene: 他长期伏案，肩颈硬得像块板，按摩几次都没用，最后去看了位老中医。 After massage failed, he went to an old doctor who treated his stiff shoulder with acupuncture.
sceneCN: 这里 acupuncture 指用针刺穴位来治疗的方法（第 1 个义项：针灸疗法）；句意为按摩无效后，他去找一位老中医做针灸。

derivatives.zh: 由 acupuncture 加 -ist 构成，义为「针灸师」
由 acu- 加 point 构成，义为「穴位」

senses.title: The medical practice
senses.definition: a system of treatment that inserts needles at defined points to relieve pain or illness
senses.definitionCN: 在特定穴位上刺入针以缓解疼痛或治疗疾病的一套疗法
senses.example: Acupuncture is covered by some health insurance plans.
senses.exampleCN: 有些医疗保险涵盖针灸。
senses.why: The word names the whole practice, needles and points together, as one branch of medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整套医术，把针与穴位合在一起，作为医学的一个分支。

senses.title: The act of needling
senses.definition: the physical insertion of needles into those points during a session
senses.definitionCN: 在治疗过程中把针刺入那些穴位的具体操作
senses.example: The acupuncture itself took only twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 针刺本身只用了二十分钟。
senses.why: The same noun can point at the hands-on act rather than the discipline, which is why it takes itself as subject.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指手上那个具体动作，而不是那门学科，所以它可以直接做主语。

intro.en: Acupuncture is a Latin-built word: needle plus puncture, named in English for a practice far older than the name.
intro.cn: acupuncture 是用拉丁语部件造出的词：针加穿刺；这门医术比这个名字古老得多。

items.en: Acus meant a needle, and also the sharp point of anything.
items.cn: acus 意为「针」，也指任何东西的尖端。

items.en: Punctura meant a pricking or a puncture, from pungere, to prick.
items.cn: punctura 意为「刺、穿孔」，出自 pungere「刺」。

items.en: The two were joined into a learned Latin term for needling.
items.cn: 两者被组合成一个学术拉丁语词，指用针刺。

items.en: English physicians coined acupuncture while writing about Far Eastern medicine.
items.cn: 英国医生在介绍远东医学的文章里造出了 acupuncture。

items.en: The word widened to cover the whole practice, its points, its needles and its clinics.
items.cn: 这个词扩展为整套医术，包含穴位、针具与诊所。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the needle root; the near-meaning group is other hands-on therapies.
note.cn: 形近组共享「针」这个词根；近义组是其他以手法施治的疗法。

entries.definition: A person trained to practise acupuncture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「针灸师」。

entries.definition: A point on the body used in acupuncture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穴位」。

entries.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小孔、穿刺」，与后半部分同源。

entries.definition: A therapy that burns dried herbs near the skin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「艾灸」，常与针灸并用。

entries.definition: Rubbing and pressing the body to relieve tension.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「按摩」，同为手法治疗。

entries.definition: Treatment by movement and physical means.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物理治疗」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into needle and puncture, then put the needle back into the clinic.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词拆成「针」与「穿刺」，再把针放回诊所里。

normal.en: Acu- means needle, so acupuncture is literally needling.
normal.cn: acu- 意为「针」，所以 acupuncture 字面上就是「用针刺」。

normal.en: The second half is the same as puncture, a small hole pricked into something.
normal.cn: 后半部分与 puncture 相同，指被刺出的小孔。

normal.en: Chinese practice is far older than the English name, which was coined in the seventeenth century.
normal.cn: 中国这门医术远比英语名字古老，后者是十七世纪才造的。

normal.en: An acupuncturist works at acupoints with fine needles, often leaving them in for twenty minutes.
normal.cn: 针灸师在穴位上用细针，常留针二十分钟。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with moxibustion, which burns herbs rather than inserting needles.
normal.cn: 别与 moxibustion 混了，后者烧的是艾草，不是把针扎进去。

abstract.en: Silver threads standing in skin like tiny masts.
abstract.cn: 银线立在皮肤上，像一根根小桅杆。

abstract.en: A shoulder that has been hard for years quietly letting go.
abstract.cn: 一只硬了许多年的肩膀，悄悄松了下来。

abstract.en: A hand that knows exactly where to place the next needle.
abstract.cn: 一只清楚下一针该落在哪里的手。

examples.en: Acupuncture helped her sleep through the pain.
examples.cn: 针灸帮她熬过了疼痛，能睡个整觉。

examples.en: He tried acupuncture after the pills stopped working.
examples.cn: 药片失效之后，他尝试了针灸。

examples.en: The clinic offers acupuncture alongside herbal medicine.
examples.cn: 这家诊所把针灸与草药并用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿Q 帮克车」——阿Q 帮人把针克在车上，一路扎到穴位

root: 由拉丁语 acus「针」与 punctura「穿刺」（出自 pungere「刺」）合成，十七世纪英语医生在介绍远东医学时造出该词；最初指针刺这一操作，后扩展为包括穴位、针具与临床的整套疗法。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the whole branch of medicine, and the particular act of inserting the needles.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：作为一门医术的针灸，以及把针真正扎进去的那一次操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine needles standing still on the skin while a tight shoulder loosens.
core.cn: 核心意象：细针稳稳立在皮肤上，紧绷的肩膀慢慢松开。

branches.en: THE INSERTION: the needle goes in at a chosen point.
branches.cn: 进针线：针在选定的穴位上刺入。

branches.en: THE SENSATION: a dull ache tells the point has been reached.
branches.cn: 针感线：一种沉沉的酸胀说明扎到了位置。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the practice gathers points, needles and training.
branches.cn: 诊所线：这套医术把穴位、针具与训练聚在一起。

branches.en: THE COURSE: treatment is repeated over weeks.
branches.cn: 疗程线：治疗要按周重复。

branches.en: THE INSURANCE: some plans pay for it as ordinary care.
branches.cn: 保险线：有些保险把它当作常规医疗来支付。

intro.en: A Latin word for needle and a Latin word for pricking were welded into one English term.
intro.cn: 一个意为「针」的拉丁词与一个意为「穿刺」的拉丁词，被焊接成一个英语术语。

latinIntro.en: Acus and punctura are both attested in Latin; the compound is a learned English coinage.
latinIntro.cn: acus 与 punctura 在拉丁语中均有文献可证；这个复合词是英语的学术造词。

items.example: It supplies the needle at the front of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词开头的「针」。

items.example: It is the source of the first element.
items.exampleCN: 它是第一个构词成分的来源。

items.example: It gives the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词的后半部分。

items.example: It is the verb behind punctura.
items.exampleCN: 它是 punctura 背后的动词。

items.example: It appears in puncture and in the second half of acupuncture.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 puncture 以及 acupuncture 的后半部分。

items.example: It keeps the pricking sense visible.
items.exampleCN: 它让「被刺」这层意思仍然可见。

items.example: It shortens acu- and joins it to point.
items.exampleCN: 它把 acu- 缩短后与 point 连在一起。

derivatives.zh: 由 acupuncture 加 -ist 构成，义为「针灸师」
由 acu- 加 point 构成，义为「穴位」

definition_zh: 总数；合计；骨料；总计的；聚集；合计
definition_en: a total formed from separate parts, or to gather separate things into one whole
core_image: 把散落的一颗颗石子倒进同一个筐里，堆成一整堆
scene: 工地旁，工人把散落的碎石一车车倒进料堆。 The workers piled the aggregate beside the road before mixing it with cement.
sceneCN: 这里 aggregate 是「骨料」（第 4 个义项：拌混凝土用的碎石等材料）；句意为工人们把骨料堆在路边，准备与水泥混合。图中可辨识物件：碎石堆、铁锹、水泥袋。

pos.zh: 名词：总数；合计；骨料；聚合体

derivatives.zh: 由 aggregate 加 -ion 构成，义为「聚集；汇总」
由 aggregate 加 -or 构成，义为「聚合者；信息聚合平台」
由 aggregate 加 -ive 构成，义为「聚合的；聚集性的」

senses.title: A total of separate parts
senses.definition: a total amount formed by adding together several separate amounts or items
senses.definitionCN: 把若干分开的数目或项目相加后得到的总量
senses.example: The aggregate of the three sales figures reached ten thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 三组销售数字合计达到一万。
senses.why: Latin grex meant a flock; aggregare was to drive animals into one herd, and the sum of parts is just such a herd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 grex 意为「群」；aggregare 是把牲畜赶成一群，而各部分相加的总数正像这样一群。

senses.title: To gather into one group
senses.definition: to bring separate people, things, or data together into a single group
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人、物或数据聚合成一个整体
senses.example: The small farms aggregate into one large cooperative.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小农场聚合成一个大合作社。
senses.why: The verb keeps the herding image: scattered units are driven into one place.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了「赶成群」的画面：散落的单位被赶到同一个地方。

senses.title: Combined as a whole
senses.definition: describing a figure or measure that is calculated from all the parts together
senses.definitionCN: 形容由全部部分共同算出的数字或尺度
senses.example: The aggregate score decided the winner of the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 总分决定了比赛的胜负。
senses.why: The adjective names the view from above, where individual items blur into one combined number.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指的是从高处看的视角，在那里个别项目模糊成一个合并的数字。

senses.title: Crushed stone for building
senses.definition: sand, gravel, or crushed stone mixed with cement to make concrete
senses.definitionCN: 与水泥混合制成混凝土的砂、砾石或碎石
senses.example: The workers piled the aggregate beside the road before mixing it with cement.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把骨料堆在路边，准备与水泥混合。
senses.why: A heap of small stones is literally an aggregate: many separate pieces gathered into one mass.
senses.whyCN: 一堆小石子本身就是字面意义上的聚合体：许多分开的碎块聚成一团。

senses.title: A mass of mixed minerals
senses.definition: a rock or mineral mass made of many separate grains or crystals
senses.definitionCN: 由许多分离的颗粒或晶体组成的岩石或矿物块
senses.example: The grey rock is an aggregate of sand and pebbles.
senses.exampleCN: 这块灰色岩石是砂与卵石的聚合体。
senses.why: Geology uses the noun for any body built of distinct grains, the literal flock of stones.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个名词指任何由不同颗粒构成的主体，正是石头的「群」。

senses.title: To amount to in total
senses.definition: to add up to a particular total when all parts are counted
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分计入后达到某个总数
senses.example: Ticket sales aggregated two million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年门票销售合计达到两百万。
senses.why: When parts are gathered in number, the verb can simply report the figure they make together.
senses.whyCN: 当各部分在数量上被聚拢，动词就可以直接报告它们合起来达到的数字。

senses.title: Totals in economic analysis
senses.definition: a whole-economy measure such as total demand or total output
senses.definitionCN: 用于整体经济的度量，如总需求或总产出
senses.example: Economists watch aggregate demand before setting interest rates.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家在设定利率之前会关注总需求。
senses.why: Economics names the summed economy by the same adjective, treating millions of choices as one flock.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用同一个形容词来指被加总的经济整体，把千百万个选择当成一群。

intro.en: Aggregate goes back to Latin grex, a flock, through the verb for driving animals into one herd.
intro.cn: aggregate 上溯到拉丁语 grex「群」，经由「把牲畜赶成一群」的动词而来。

items.en: Grex meant a flock or herd, the image behind several English words about groups.
items.cn: grex 意为「群、群畜」，是英语中若干表示群体的词的画面来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus gregare 'to herd' made aggregare, to drive together into one flock.
items.cn: ad-「向」加上 gregare「赶群」构成 aggregare，意为「赶成一群」。

items.en: The participle aggregatus described things gathered into a single mass.
items.cn: 分词 aggregatus 描述被聚成一体的东西。

items.en: English borrowed the word for a sum of separate items, and later for a heap of stones.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词指分开项目的总和，后来又指一堆石子。

items.en: Building and economics gave the word its technical senses: concrete aggregate and aggregate demand.
items.cn: 建筑与经济学赋予它专业含义：混凝土骨料与总需求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for totals and wholes.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词与形容词；近义组收表示总数与整体的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or result of gathering things into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聚集；汇总」，指把事物聚成整体的行为或结果。

entries.definition: A person or service that collects information or offers from many sources.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聚合者；聚合平台」，指从多方收集信息或商品的人或服务。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning tending to gather things into a group.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聚合性的；倾向于聚集的」。

entries.definition: The whole amount obtained by adding all the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「总数；总额」，指全部部分相加所得的整体。

entries.definition: The result of adding two or more numbers or amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「和；总数」，指两个或多个数目相加的结果。

entries.definition: A complete thing made of all its parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「整体；全部」，指由全部部分构成的完整事物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to herds, heaps of stone and the act of adding up.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与群、石堆以及加总动作联系起来。

normal.en: AGGREGATE contains 'greg', the Latin word for a flock: many animals driven into one group.
normal.cn: aggregate 里有 greg，拉丁语指「群」：许多动物被赶成一群。

normal.en: Picture a heap of gravel gathered from many small piles.
normal.cn: 想象一堆砾石，是从许多小堆聚拢来的。

normal.en: Think of a scoreboard that adds every game into one aggregate score.
normal.cn: 想一块记分牌，把每场比赛加成一个总分。

normal.en: Concrete is stone plus cement: the stone part is the aggregate.
normal.cn: 混凝土是石子加水泥：石子那部分就是骨料。

normal.en: In the aggregate means 'seen as one heap, not one by one'.
normal.cn: in the aggregate 的意思就是「当成一堆看，而不是一件件看」。

abstract.en: An aggregate hides its parts the way a crowd hides its faces.
abstract.cn: 总量像人群遮住面孔那样，把各个部分遮了起来。

abstract.en: The word begins with animals and ends with economies.
abstract.cn: 这个词从牲畜开始，最后落在经济总量上。

abstract.en: Every total is a decision about which parts to count.
abstract.cn: 每一个总数，都是关于「算进哪些部分」的一次决定。

examples.en: The aggregate of all donations paid for the new clinic.
examples.cn: 所有捐款的合计支付了新诊所的费用。

examples.en: Researchers aggregated data from twenty hospitals.
examples.cn: 研究人员汇总了二十家医院的数据。

examples.en: The team lost on aggregate despite winning the second match.
examples.cn: 尽管赢下第二场比赛，球队仍按总分落败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「挨个归集」：把东西挨个归到一起，就得到总数。

root: 拉丁语 grex（群）加前缀 ad- 构成 aggregare（赶成一群），过去分词 aggregatus 进入英语，核心是「把分散的部分聚成一个整体」，由此生出「总数」与「骨料」等义。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a sum of parts to the act of gathering, then to combined measures, heaps of stone, mineral masses and economic totals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从各部分之和走到聚集动作，再到合并的度量、石堆、矿物集合体与经济总量。

core.en: PARTS GATHERED INTO ONE
core.cn: 把各部分聚成一体

branches.en: parts added into a total
branches.cn: 各部分相加成总数

branches.en: the act of gathering
branches.cn: 聚集的动作

branches.en: a combined measure seen from above
branches.cn: 从高处看的合并度量

branches.en: stone gathered for building
branches.cn: 为建筑聚起的石子

branches.en: grains gathered into rock
branches.cn: 颗粒聚成的岩石

intro.en: Aggregate belongs to the grex family, whose words all picture groups, herds or gatherings.
intro.cn: aggregate 属于 grex 词族，这一族的词都描绘群体、畜群或聚集。

latinIntro.en: Latin grex gives the base; ad- and -atus build the verb and participle, and English adds -ion, -or, -ive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 grex 提供词基；ad- 与 -atus 造出动词与分词，英语再加 -ion、-or、-ive。

items.meaning: the act or result of gathering into a whole
items.example: The aggregation of small datasets revealed a clear trend.
items.exampleCN: 小数据集的汇总揭示出清晰的趋势。

items.meaning: one that collects things from many sources
items.example: The news aggregator lists stories from many papers.
items.exampleCN: 这个新闻聚合平台列出许多报纸的报道。

items.meaning: tending to gather into a group
items.example: The aggregative habit of the ants protects the colony.
items.exampleCN: 蚂蚁的聚集习性保护了整个群体。

items.example: She is a gregarious host who loves a full room.
items.exampleCN: 她是个爱热闹的主人，喜欢满屋子客人。

items.meaning: to come together in a crowd
items.example: Families congregate in the square each evening.
items.exampleCN: 每到傍晚，各家各户都聚到广场上。

items.meaning: to separate one group from another
items.example: The old rules segregated the students by sex.
items.exampleCN: 旧规矩按性别把学生隔开。

items.meaningCN: 极其恶劣的；令人震惊的
items.example: The report described an egregious error.
items.exampleCN: 报告描述了一处极其严重的错误。

items.meaning: the total demand for goods in an economy
items.example: Aggregate demand fell after the price rise.
items.exampleCN: 价格上涨后总需求下降了。

latinEntries.meaning: to drive together into a flock

definition_zh: 中止；使夭折；流产；放弃
definition_en: to stop a plan, process, or operation before it is finished, or to end a pregnancy early
core_image: 一枚刚点火的火箭在半空突然熄火，掉头落回地面
scene: 控制室里的倒计时走到一半，屏幕上跳出红色警告，工程师们把手从按钮上移开。 The launch was aborted ten seconds before lift-off.
sceneCN: 这里 abort 指中止发射任务（第 2 个义项：中止技术操作）；句意为发射在升空前十秒被中止。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「流产；堕胎；中途失败」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词与拉丁词干合成，义为「堕胎药」，也可作形容词

senses.title: To stop a plan before it is finished
senses.definition: to end a plan or project deliberately while it is still under way
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或项目仍在进行时有意将其终止
senses.example: The company aborted the expansion after the first survey.
senses.exampleCN: 第一轮调研之后，公司中止了扩张计划。
senses.why: The Latin verb described a birth that stops before its time, and a plan can stop before its time in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词描述未足月就停止的分娩，计划也可以同样未到时辰就停住。

senses.title: To cancel a launch or operation
senses.definition: to stop a launch, flight, or technical operation before or during its start
senses.definitionCN: 在发射、飞行或技术操作开始前或开始过程中将其停止
senses.example: The launch was aborted ten seconds before lift-off.
senses.exampleCN: 发射在升空前十秒被中止。
senses.why: Mission control needs one word that means everything stops now, and this is that word.
senses.whyCN: 任务控制需要一个词表示「现在就全部停下」，用的正是这个词。

senses.title: To end a pregnancy deliberately
senses.definition: in medicine, to end a pregnancy by a medical procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在医学上，通过医疗手段终止妊娠
senses.example: The clinic provides counselling before a patient decides to abort.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所会在病人决定终止妊娠之前提供咨询。
senses.why: The medical sense is the oldest surviving one, and it keeps the plain meaning of a process stopped early.
senses.whyCN: 医学义是留存下来的最古老含义，它保留了「过程提前停止」这一朴素意义。

senses.title: To miscarry naturally
senses.definition: of a pregnancy, to end on its own before the fetus can survive
senses.definitionCN: 指妊娠在胎儿能够存活之前自行结束
senses.example: The ewe aborted in the cold snap and had to be watched closely.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮中那只母羊流产了，得密切观察。
senses.why: Before it named an operation, the word simply reported that a pregnancy had not reached its term.
senses.whyCN: 在指手术之前，这个词只是报告一次妊娠没有到足月。

intro.en: Abort began as a word about a birth that never reached its term, and every later sense is a process stopped before its proper end.
intro.cn: abort 最初说的是没有到足月的生产，之后每一个义项都是「在应有的终点之前停住的过程」。

items.en: Modern use extends from medicine to computing and spaceflight, always with the sense of a deliberate stop.
items.cn: 现代用法从医学延伸到计算机与航天，始终带有「有意停止」的意味。

items.en: English took the verb from Latin in the sixteenth century, first in the medical sense of a pregnancy ending early.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，最初用于妊娠提前结束的医学义。

items.en: Abortus was the noun for a miscarriage, and abortiri was the deponent verb meaning to miscarry or fail.
items.cn: abortus 是表示流产的名词，abortiri 则是意为「流产、失败」的异态动词。

items.en: The verb was built from ab- meaning away and oriri meaning to rise or be born, so it pictured a rising that never happened.
items.cn: 这个动词由表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「升起、出生」的 oriri 构成，画面是一次没有发生的升起。

items.en: Oriri also gave English orient and origin, both naming a beginning or a rising point.
items.cn: oriri 还给英语带来了 orient 与 origin，两者都指开端或升起的起点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for stopping something that has already begun.
note.cn: 形近组收建在同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示停止已开始之事的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an early end to a pregnancy, or a plan that failed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流产、堕胎」，也指中途失败的计划。

entries.definition: Failing to produce the intended result, as in an abortive attempt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「夭折的、失败的」，如 abortive attempt。

entries.definition: A drug or substance that causes a pregnancy to end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堕胎药」，也可作形容词指「引起流产的」。

entries.definition: Stopped before completion, as in an aborted launch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中止的、未完成的」，如 aborted launch。

entries.definition: To decide that a planned event or order will not happen at all.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取消」，指决定原定的事不发生。

entries.definition: To cancel an event or an operation, often at short notice.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「取消」，常在临近时叫停。

entries.definition: To bring something to an end, especially a contract or a process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「终止」，多用于合同或进程。

entries.definition: To lose a pregnancy naturally before the fetus can survive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「自然流产」，指胎儿未能存活前妊娠自行结束。

entries.definition: To abandon a plan or project completely, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废弃、放弃」，口语中指彻底丢开计划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the birth image inside the Latin root and the technical settings where the word now appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁词根里「出生」的形象，以及这个词今天出现的各种技术场景。

normal.en: The Latin parts are ab- meaning away and oriri meaning to rise, so abort is a rising that is called off.
normal.cn: 拉丁构件是表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「升起」的 oriri，所以 abort 是一次被叫停的升起。

normal.en: Origin and orient come from the same oriri, all three words about a beginning or a rising point.
normal.cn: origin 与 orient 出自同一个 oriri，三个词都关于开端或升起的起点。

normal.en: In mission control the single word abort means everything stops now.
normal.cn: 在任务控制里，单个词 abort 意思是「现在全部停下」。

normal.en: A computer aborts a process the way a rocket aborts a launch: before the planned end.
normal.cn: 计算机中止进程，就像火箭中止发射：都在预定的终点之前停住。

normal.en: Abortive describes the attempt that failed, and aborted describes the thing that was stopped.
normal.cn: abortive 描述失败了的尝试，aborted 描述被中止了的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a countdown frozen at the last second, the engine lit but the rocket still on the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象倒计时停在最后一秒，引擎已经点火，火箭却仍留在发射台上。

abstract.en: The same frozen countdown appears in an operating theatre and in a program waiting for a signal.
abstract.cn: 同一个被冻住的倒计时，也出现在手术室和等待信号的程序里。

abstract.en: Every use is a flight cut short, and the word is about the cut, not about the crash.
abstract.cn: 每一次用法都是一次被截短的飞行，这个词讲的是那一刀，而不是坠毁。

examples.en: The crew aborted the mission when the fuel reading fell.
examples.cn: 燃料读数下降时，机组中止了任务。

examples.en: The software will abort the download if the file is corrupted.
examples.cn: 如果文件损坏，软件会中止下载。

examples.en: They aborted the trial after the first results were clearly negative.
examples.cn: 首批结果明显为负面后，他们中止了试验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，波特」——波特在倒计时最后一秒按下停止，火箭没有起飞

root: 拉丁语 abortiri「流产、失败」← ab-「离开」＋ oriri「升起、出生」，字面即「未能升起」；名词 abortus 指流产。同根还产生 origin 与 orient。英语十六世纪借入，先为医学义，后扩展到任务与计算机。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses stop three kinds of process early: a plan, a launch or operation, a pregnancy, and a natural pregnancy loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项分别提前叫停计划、发射或操作、妊娠，以及自然发生的流产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a countdown stops at the last second and the rocket never rises.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒计时停在最后一秒，火箭始终没有升起。

branches.en: THE PLAN: something is called off before it matures.
branches.cn: 计划线：事情还没成熟就被叫停。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: a launch or procedure is cut off midway.
branches.cn: 操作线：发射或程序在中途被切断。

branches.en: THE PREGNANCY: the medical ending of a pregnancy.
branches.cn: 医学线：在医学上终止妊娠。

branches.en: THE NATURAL LOSS: the body ends a pregnancy without help.
branches.cn: 自然线：身体在没有外力介入时终止妊娠。

branches.en: THE EARLY STOP: every sense is a halt before completion.
branches.cn: 中止线：每个义项都是在完成之前停住。

intro.en: The word is Latin plus a plain English verb ending, and the two Latin parts still explain every sense.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语加一个普通英语动词词尾，两个拉丁部件至今能解释每一个义项。

latinIntro.en: Latin abortus, abortiri, and oriri are recorded, so no part of the word needs reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abortus、abortiri 与 oriri 都有文献记录，这个词没有任何部件需要重构。

items.example: It marks the rising that does not happen.
items.exampleCN: 它标记那一次没有发生的升起。

items.example: It also gives origin and orient.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生了 origin 与 orient。

items.example: It is the Latin verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: It is the noun that gave abortion.
items.exampleCN: 它正是产生 abortion 的名词。

items.example: It entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 它在十六世纪进入英语。

definition_zh: 使隶属；使加入；加入；附属机构
definition_en: to officially join or connect an organization with a larger one; a company or group that is linked to a larger organization
core_image: 一根细枝接到主干上：小机构挂进大体系
scene: 城市的街角，几个独立的小工作室共用一块招牌，也共用同一套培训。 The small studio chose to affiliate with a national network.
sceneCN: 这里 affiliate 是「加入、隶属」（第 1 个义项：正式加入一个更大的组织）；句意为这家小工作室选择加入一个全国性的网络。画面中可辨识：共用招牌、工作室、培训手册。

derivatives.zh: 由 affiliate 加 -ion 构成，义为「隶属关系；加入；归属」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「附属的；有关联的」
由 dis- 加 affiliate 构成，义为「退出；脱离隶属关系」

senses.title: To connect an organization with a larger one
senses.definition: to officially attach a person or organization to a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 正式把个人或组织附属于一个更大的团体
senses.example: The clinic agreed to affiliate itself with the university hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所同意隶属于那所大学医院。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to adopt as a son, so the modern sense keeps the image of taking a smaller unit into a family.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「收为养子」，现代义保留了把较小单位收进一个家族的形象。

senses.title: To join or become linked
senses.definition: to join a larger group or form a working link with it, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 加入一个更大的团体或与其建立工作联系，作不及物动词
senses.example: Several local clubs affiliate with the national association each year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年都有几个本地俱乐部加入这个全国协会。
senses.why: Once the smaller unit can act for itself, the verb turns intransitive: it chooses to join.
senses.whyCN: 当较小单位能自行行动时，这个动词就转为不及物：它自己选择加入。

senses.title: A linked organization
senses.definition: a company, club, or group that is officially connected to a larger organization
senses.definitionCN: 正式与更大组织相连的公司、俱乐部或团体
senses.example: The radio station is a local affiliate of the national network.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台是该全国网络的本地附属台。
senses.why: The verb's object becomes a noun: the unit that has been taken into the family.
senses.whyCN: 动词的宾语转成名词：那个被收进家族的单位。

senses.title: To establish a legal link of parentage
senses.definition: in law, to establish the legal relationship of a child to a parent, or to assign something to a source
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上确立子女与父母之间的亲子关系，或把某物归属于某一来源
senses.example: The court affiliated the child to the man named in the will.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这个孩子与遗嘱中所写的那名男子存在父子关系。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense surviving almost unchanged: to declare that someone belongs to a particular father.
senses.whyCN: 这是几乎原样保留的最古老义项：宣告某人属于某位父亲。

intro.en: Affiliate began as a legal word about sons and only later became a word about organizations.
intro.cn: affiliate 起初是关于儿子的法律词，后来才变成关于组织的词。

items.en: Filius meant 'son', and the whole family of the word grows from that single noun.
items.cn: filius 意为「儿子」，整个词族都从这个名词生长出来。

items.en: Affiliare meant 'to adopt as a son', formed with ad- 'to' and filius.
items.cn: affiliare 意为「收为养子」，由 ad-「向」与 filius 构成。

items.en: Medieval legal Latin used affiliatus for a child legally assigned to a father.
items.cn: 中世纪法律拉丁语用 affiliatus 指在法律上归属于某位父亲的孩子。

items.en: English extended the word from family law to the joining of societies and institutions.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从家庭法扩展到社团与机构的加入。

items.en: Business and media gave the noun affiliate its everyday sense of a linked local branch.
items.cn: 商业与传媒赋予名词 affiliate 今天的日常义：有关联的本地分支。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin 'son' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of joining and attachment.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「儿子」词根的一族词；近义组收表示加入与附属的动词和名词。

entries.definition: The state of being officially connected to a larger group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「隶属关系；归属」，由 affiliate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Officially connected with or controlled by a larger organization.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附属的；有关联的」，是 affiliate 的过去分词。

entries.definition: Relating to a son or daughter and the duty owed to parents.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「子女的；孝顺的」，与 affiliate 同出拉丁语 filius「儿子」。

entries.definition: To join or fasten one thing to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「附上；连接」，可指物理连接，也可指关系上的归属。

entries.definition: To connect people or organizations in a working relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使联合；使关联」，语气比 affiliate 更宽泛。

entries.definition: To become a member of a group or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加入」，最通用，不强调大小机构之间的隶属。

entries.definition: A company owned or controlled by a larger company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「子公司；附属公司」，与义项三相近，但强调所有权。

normalIntro.en: Affiliate is anchored by the Latin word for son and by the modern image of a branch joining a tree.
normalIntro.cn: affiliate 可以靠拉丁语「儿子」这个词，以及树枝接到树干上的现代意象来记。

normal.en: Filius means son, so affiliate first meant to adopt as a son.
normal.cn: filius 意为「儿子」，所以 affiliate 最初指「收为养子」。

normal.en: An affiliate is a unit taken into a larger family and given its name.
normal.cn: affiliate 就是被收进更大体系并挂上其名号的单位。

normal.en: Be affiliated with is the phrase you will see in forms and official descriptions.
normal.cn: be affiliated with 是表格和官方介绍里常见的说法。

normal.en: Affiliation is the noun for the link itself, not for the unit.
normal.cn: affiliation 指联系本身，而不是那个单位。

normal.en: Disaffiliate is its opposite: to leave the family.
normal.cn: disaffiliate 是它的反义：离开这个家族。

abstract.en: Picture a small branch grafted onto a strong trunk, keeping its own leaves but sharing the root.
abstract.cn: 想象一根小枝嫁接到粗壮的树干上，保留自己的叶子，却共享同一个根。

abstract.en: Think of a local radio station carrying a national logo on its sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一家本地电台在招牌上挂着全国网络的标志。

abstract.en: See the word as a door: joining means walking through it and taking the larger house's name.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一扇门：加入就是走进去，并冠上大房子的姓氏。

examples.en: The research centre is affiliated with a major university.
examples.cn: 这个研究中心隶属于一所重点大学。

examples.en: The local newspaper became an affiliate of the national chain.
examples.cn: 这家本地报纸成了全国报业连锁的附属机构。

examples.en: Members voted to leave the association last spring.
examples.cn: 成员们在去年春天投票决定退出该协会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲利特」——阿（a）菲（fei）利（li）特（te），小机构特别想依附大网络。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 filius「儿子」构成 affiliare「收为养子」，中世纪法律拉丁语 affiliatus 指法律上归属某位父亲的孩子；作名词时读「/əˈfɪliət/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word travels from family law to institutional life: adopt a son, join a group, become a branch, and finally declare a legal parent.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从家庭法走到机构生活：收为养子、加入团体、成为分支，最后仍保留宣告法律父关系的一义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch grafted onto a trunk
core.cn: 核心意象：一根嫁接到树干上的枝条

branches.en: A larger body takes a smaller one into its family.
branches.cn: 较大机构把较小单位收进自己的家族。

branches.en: The smaller unit chooses to join on its own.
branches.cn: 较小单位自行选择加入。

branches.en: The joined unit itself, now a named branch.
branches.cn: 被收进的单位本身，如今是有名号的分支。

branches.en: The oldest legal sense: declaring a parental link.
branches.cn: 最古老的法律义：宣告亲子关系。

branches.en: Attachment seen from the larger and the smaller side.
branches.cn: 从大机构与小机构两个视角看同一种附属关系。

intro.en: Affiliate is a Latin legal construction whose parts still explain affiliation and filial.
intro.cn: affiliate 是拉丁语法律构词，其成分仍能解释 affiliation 与 filial。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus filius produced affiliare; the noun filius also gave English filial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 filius 构成 affiliare；名词 filius 还给了英语 filial。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Filius is the root of affiliate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: filius 是 affiliate 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affiliare entered law and then business.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affiliare 先进入法律，后进入商业。

definition_zh: 折磨；使痛苦；使苦恼；（疾病）侵袭
definition_en: to cause pain, suffering, or distress to someone, often repeatedly or over a long period
core_image: 一记反复落下的打击，让人长期受苦
scene: 雨季里，村庄的道路被洪水冲断，病人要走很远才能找到医生。 Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
sceneCN: 这里 afflicted 是「折磨、使受苦」（第 1 个义项：给身体或精神带来持续痛苦）；句意为慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。画面中可辨识：被冲断的道路、拄杖的病人、远处的诊所。

derivatives.zh: 由 afflict 加 -ion 构成，义为「痛苦；苦难；折磨人的病痛」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「受折磨的；患病的」
由 afflict 加 -ive 构成，义为「令人痛苦的；造成苦难的」

senses.title: To cause pain or suffering
senses.definition: to cause pain or suffering to a person or group, especially over time
senses.definitionCN: 给人或群体带来痛苦或苦难，尤指持续性的
senses.example: Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to strike something down, so suffering is pictured as blow after blow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「击倒」，所以苦难被想象成一记接一记的打击。

senses.title: Of a disease: to attack
senses.definition: of an illness or condition, to attack a person or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或病症侵袭某人或身体某部位
senses.example: A rare skin disease afflicted the workers in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 一种罕见的皮肤病侵袭了那座旧工厂里的工人。
senses.why: A disease arrives like a series of blows the body cannot ward off, which is why the verb fits illness so well.
senses.whyCN: 疾病到来就像身体挡不住的一连串打击，所以这个动词特别适合描述疾病。

senses.title: To bring hardship to a place or group
senses.definition: to cause hardship, disaster, or serious difficulty for a place or community
senses.definitionCN: 给某地或某群体带来困苦、灾难或严重困难
senses.example: Drought and failed harvests afflicted the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱和歉收让整个地区陷入苦难。
senses.why: The blows can fall on a whole community, not only on one body, so the word extends to shared hardship.
senses.whyCN: 打击可以落在整个社区而不只是一个人身上，于是这个词扩展到共同的苦难。

senses.title: To trouble the mind
senses.definition: to distress or trouble someone mentally, especially with worry or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 在精神上使某人痛苦或困扰，尤指忧虑与疑虑
senses.example: Doubts about the decision afflicted her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个决定的疑虑折磨了她好几个星期。
senses.why: What strikes the body can also strike the mind, and this sense names the inward version of the same pain.
senses.whyCN: 打击身体的东西也能打击心灵，这个义项指的是同一种痛苦转向内心的形态。

intro.en: Afflict comes from Latin verbs of striking, and its core image is a blow that keeps falling.
intro.cn: afflict 来自拉丁语表示「打击」的动词，核心意象是一记不断落下的打击。

items.en: Fligere meant 'to strike, dash', and it also lies behind conflict.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击、猛撞」，它也是 conflict 的词源成分。

items.en: Affligere meant 'to dash down, strike against, ruin', built with ad- and fligere.
items.cn: affligere 意为「击倒、撞击、毁坏」，由 ad- 与 fligere 构成。

items.en: The frequentative afflictare meant 'to keep striking, harass, torment'.
items.cn: 反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断打击、骚扰、折磨」。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin participle afflictus, partly through French, as the verb afflict.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入拉丁语分词 afflictus，形成动词 afflict。

items.en: The medical and mental senses settled beside the older sense of external hardship.
items.cn: 医学义与精神义在较早的「外在困苦」义旁稳定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'strike' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of causing pain and hardship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「打击」词根的一族词；近义组收造成痛苦与困苦的动词。

entries.definition: A condition of pain, suffering, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「痛苦；苦难；病痛」，由 afflict 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Suffering from pain, illness, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受折磨的；患病的」，是 afflict 的过去分词。

entries.definition: A serious disagreement or a fight between opposing forces.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲突；争斗」，与 afflict 同出拉丁语 fligere「打击」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone severe and lasting suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「折磨」，痛苦程度比 afflict 更重，常带持续性。

entries.definition: To cause continual trouble or distress to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不断困扰；使遭灾」，强调反复与恼人。

entries.definition: To make someone feel very worried, unhappy, or uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使痛苦；使忧虑」，侧重情绪上的难受。

normalIntro.en: Afflict is held by the image of a strike and by its large family of nouns and adjectives.
normalIntro.cn: afflict 可以靠「打击」这个意象，以及它成串的名词与形容词来记。

normal.en: Fligere means strike, so afflict is to strike someone down with pain.
normal.cn: fligere 意为「打击」，所以 afflict 就是用痛苦把人击倒。

normal.en: Affliction is the pain itself, and afflicted describes the person who carries it.
normal.cn: affliction 是痛苦本身，afflicted 描述承受痛苦的人。

normal.en: Be afflicted with is the passive phrase used for illness and hardship.
normal.cn: be afflicted with 是用于疾病与困苦的被动搭配。

normal.en: Conflict shares the same strike root but adds a different prefix meaning together.
normal.cn: conflict 共享同一「打击」词根，只是前缀表示「共同」。

normal.en: Afflictive is the adjective for whatever causes the suffering.
normal.cn: afflictive 是形容造成痛苦之物的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer that keeps falling on the same spot, never quite stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锤子反复落在同一个地方，始终停不下来。

abstract.en: Think of a weight carried on the shoulders for years, invisible to others.
abstract.cn: 想象一副在肩上压了多年的重担，别人却看不见。

abstract.en: See the word as rain that will not stop: at first it is weather, then it becomes hardship.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一场停不下来的雨：起初只是天气，后来就成了苦难。

examples.en: The region has been afflicted by drought for three years.
examples.cn: 这个地区已经遭受旱灾三年。

examples.en: She was afflicted with a severe headache before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她饱受剧烈头痛的折磨。

examples.en: The village rebuilt its bridge the following spring.
examples.cn: 村庄在第二年春天重建了桥梁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗利克特」——阿（a）弗（fu）利（li）克（ke）特（te），一记记打击不断落在身上。

root: 拉丁语 fligere「打击」加前缀 ad- 构成 affligere「击倒」，其反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断折磨」，英语借入分词形式 afflictus。

sensesIntro.en: One image of repeated blows expands outward: physical pain, disease, communal hardship, and finally mental trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 「反复打击」这一意象向外扩展：身体疼痛、疾病、群体困苦，最后是精神上的困扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blow after blow falling on the same spot
core.cn: 核心意象：一记接一记落在同一处的打击

branches.en: Pain pictured as repeated blows.
branches.cn: 把痛苦想象成反复的打击。

branches.en: A disease delivering those blows.
branches.cn: 疾病送来这些打击。

branches.en: The blows landing on a whole community.
branches.cn: 打击落在整个社区身上。

branches.en: The same blows turned inward on the mind.
branches.cn: 同样的打击转向内心。

branches.en: Pain for one body and hardship for a group.
branches.cn: 一个人的疼痛与一群人的困苦。

intro.en: Afflict is built from a prefix and a Latin root of striking, and its family is mostly suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: afflict 由前缀与表示「打击」的拉丁词根构成，其词族主要是同一词干加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fligere gave affligere, and the participle afflictus gave English its stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fligere 构成 affligere，分词 afflictus 为英语提供了词干。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fligere is the root of afflict and conflict.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fligere 是 afflict 与 conflict 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Afflictare strengthened the sense of repeated pain.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afflictare 强化了反复痛苦的含义。
